brief_summary: Thoracic hyperkyphosis is a prevalent postural deformity characterized by an excessiveposteriorcurvature of the thoracic spine, typically defined by a Cobb angle greater than 40degrees.Itisincreasingly common among adolescents and young adults due to prolonged sedentarybehavior,poorpostural habits, extensive use of electronic devices, and reduced ergonomic awareness, whichcontributeto progressive spinal deformity and associated complications such as chronic back pain, reducedspinalflexibility, impaired respiratory function, and diminished quality of life (1, 2, 8, 11). Conventionalphysiotherapy approaches, including generalized strengthening, stretching, and postural education,oftenprovide symptomatic relief but fail to adequately address the three-dimensional natureofspinaldeformities or produce lasting structural correction (1, 2, 20). The Schroth method, aspecializedphysiotherapeutic intervention, emphasizes three-dimensional corrective exercises, rotational breathing,and postural awareness to realign the spine, reduce abnormal curvature, improve muscular symmetry,andenhance functional capacity (15, 18, 21). This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of Schroththerapyin reducing thoracic Cobb angle, alleviating postural back pain, and improving spinal rangeof motioninpatients with thoracic hyperkyphosis, compared to conventional physiotherapy.
primary_outcomes: Thoracic Range of Motion (Goniometer and Bubble Inclinometer)
title: Effects of Schroth Therapy on Pain, Range of Motion and Cobb Angle in Patients With Postural Hyperkyphosis.

brief_summary:
spinning top activities are play-based fine motor exercises that involve rotating and controlling a spinning top using finger and hand movements. These activities may improve fine motor coordination, finger dexterity, hand-eye coordination, visual-motor integration, and hand muscle control.

Regular practice of spinning top activities may help school-going children develop better pencil grip, finger movements, hand stability, and motor control, which are important for handwriting performance. These activities may also improve handwriting speed, legibility, letter formation, and overall writing efficiency.

brief_summary:
Joint replacement surgery, including total hip replacement and total knee replacement, may be followed by postoperative pain, sleep disturbances, and fear of movement (kinesiophobia), which can interfere with recovery and rehabilitation. Progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) is a non-pharmacological technique that involves gently tensing and relaxing different muscle groups while maintaining comfortable breathing.

This study evaluated the effect of a nurse-led progressive muscle relaxation technique on pain intensity, sleep quality, and kinesiophobia among adults undergoing joint replacement surgery. The study included 60 adult patients undergoing primary total hip or total knee replacement at Damanhour National Medical Institute, Al-Beheira Governorate, Egypt. Participants were allocated to an intervention group (30 patients) or a control group (30 patients).

The intervention group received nurse-led PMR in addition to routine postoperative care, while the control group received routine postoperative care alone. The PMR intervention consisted of individual sessions lasting approximately 20-30 minutes, delivered three times daily for three consecutive days, from postoperative day 3 through postoperative day 5.

Pain intensity, sleep quality, and kinesiophobia were assessed before and after the intervention using standardised assessment scales. The study hypothesised that patients receiving nurse-led PMR in addition to routine postoperative care would experience lower pain intensity, better sleep quality, and less fear of movement than patients receiving routine postoperative care alone.
interventions: Nurse-Led Progressive Muscle Relaxation plus Routine Care
primary_outcomes: Effect of Nurse-Led Progressive Muscle Relaxation Technique on Postoperative Pain
title: Nurse-Led Progressive Muscle Relaxation for Pain, Sleep Quality, and Kinesiophobia After Joint Replacement Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether treatment adjustments guided by an early diffusion-weighted magnetic-resonance imaging (DWI-MRI) scan work better than standard care for adults with locally advanced stage III non-small cell lung cancer who are scheduled to receive definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy. This study also evaluates the safety of this DWI-MRI-guided adaptive treatment strategy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does DWI-MRI-guided early treatment adjustment bring better tumor response for participants after concurrent chemoradiotherapy?
* Can this adaptive-treatment approach help participants live longer without cancer progression?

Standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy is the established treatment for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer. Currently, tumor response is mostly assessed by computed tomography (CT) only after the full course of chemoradiotherapy is finished. This late assessment cannot identify participants with poor early treatment response during therapy. Diffusion-weighted magnetic-resonance imaging (DWI-MRI) is a specialized MRI technique. It can detect tumor cellular changes earlier than conventional CT scans. However, high-level evidence from prospective randomized trials is still lacking to confirm whether adjusting treatment based on early DWI-MRI findings improves patient outcomes.

Researchers will compare two study groups. All participants will be assigned by stratified random assignment. Stratification factors include cancer stage subgroups, pathological type, and planned consolidation immunotherapy. Image evaluators and statistical analysts will remain blind to group assignment. One group will receive an early-phase DWI-MRI scan during treatment to support adaptive treatment decisions. The other group will receive standard care without this early DWI-MRI evaluation.

Participants will:

* Receive standard definitive concurrent radiation and platinum-based double-agent chemotherapy for lung cancer.
* Complete baseline chest DWI-MRI scans within four weeks before starting chemoradiotherapy. This baseline scan provides tumor measurements for later comparison.
* Be randomly placed into one of the two groups after signing written informed consent and completing screening.
* For participants in the DWI-MRI-guided group: complete an additional DWI-MRI scan at week 3 of chemoradiotherapy (plus or minus three days), when about 20 %-30 % of total radiation dose has been delivered. An independent imaging review team will assess ADC changes from DWI-MRI without knowing group information. If early tumor response is poor, a multi-disciplinary team will discuss possible treatment adjustments, such as adaptive radiation replanning, regional radiation dose escalation, chemotherapy modification or enhanced supportive care. If response is good, participants keep their original treatment plan.
* For participants in the standard-care group: no extra week-3 DWI-MRI scan during chemoradiotherapy. Their first tumor-response evaluation will use routine CT scans approximately one month after chemoradiotherapy ends, and subsequent treatment decisions will be made according to these CT results.
* Attend regular clinic visits for physical examinations, blood laboratory tests and required imaging studies. Any new health problems will be recorded at each visit.
* Complete health-status follow-up every three months for up to 36 months after enrollment. Researchers will collect information on tumor status, subsequent anti-cancer treatments and survival conditions.
* Report any new uncomfortable symptoms or health issues to study doctors between scheduled visits.

This trial will collect data on tumor response, survival outcomes and treatment-related adverse events graded per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events. The comparison between groups will show whether DWI-MRI-driven adaptive treatment offers clinical benefits for participants with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Air Force Medical University
title: Diffusion-Weighted MRI-Guided Early Response Assessment and Adaptive Therapy for Stage Ⅲ Locally Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.

brief_summary:
Earthquakes disrupt healthcare services and increase the healthcare needs of pregnant women, women in labor, and newborns. Providing safe delivery care in these conditions requires midwives to assess mothers and newborns, identify obstetric risks, manage delivery, and provide postpartum care despite limited resources. The Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for Sexual and Reproductive Health aims to prevent avoidable maternal and neonatal illness and deaths during crises. Midwifery students need appropriate knowledge and practical skills to manage delivery during earthquakes. Gamification and escape room activities may support active learning and practical skill development.

The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effects of gamified delivery management training, developed within the MISP framework, on midwifery students' knowledge, practical skills, and self-efficacy. The study will include 60 fourth-year midwifery students (30 in each group) from the University of Health Sciences, Gülhane Faculty of Health Sciences. Participants must be enrolled in the seventh semester, have successfully completed normal and high-risk delivery courses, and agree to participate voluntarily.

Researchers will compare gamified hybrid training with scenario-based simulation training. The intervention group will use a digital escape room developed with the ActionBound platform and complete hands-on skills stations. The control group will receive the same content and training time without gamification. Both groups will receive 360 minutes of training. The training will cover six areas: initial maternal assessment, obstetric triage, preparation of the 6A Kit, delivery management, assessment of uterine tone and postpartum bleeding, and initial newborn assessment.

Participants' knowledge and self-efficacy will be assessed before training, immediately after training, and at one- and three-month follow-ups. Knowledge will be measured using a 30-item questionnaire, and self-efficacy will be assessed using the Sherer Self-Efficacy Scale. Practical skills will be evaluated after training through a four-station Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). The main outcomes are post-training practical skills and changes in knowledge over three months. Changes in self-efficacy will be assessed as a secondary outcome.

The study aims to determine whether gamified hybrid training improves students' knowledge, practical skills, and self-efficacy more than simulation-based training. The findings may support the integration of MISP principles into midwifery education and help prepare future midwives to provide safe delivery care during earthquakes.
conditions: Gamified Training on Delivery Management During Earthquakes Within the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) Framework
interventions: Experimental: Gamified MISP-Based Training in Delivery Management in Earthquake Settings
active comparator: hands-on delivery education through scenario-based simulation
primary_outcomes: Change in Midwifery Students' Delivery Management Skills During Earthquakes
Change in Midwifery Students' Knowledge of Triage and Delivery Management During Earthquakes
Change in Midwifery Students' Self-Efficacy Levels
title: The Effect of Gamified Training on Delivery Management During an Earthquake on the Knowledge, Skills, and Self-Efficacy Levels of Midwifery Students

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether Pf bacteriophage (phage) status can be used as a predictive biomarker to guide antibiotic selection and improve treatment response in adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis and chronic Pf phage-positive Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway infection. Participants must be at least 12 years of age and have chronic P. aeruginosa infection with detectable Pf bacteriophage in sputum.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does treatment with oral ciprofloxacin result in greater improvement in lung function (FEV1) than inhaled tobramycin in participants with Pf phage-positive P. aeruginosa infection?
* Can Pf phage status predict clinical and microbiologic response to antibiotic therapy, including changes in bacterial density, airway inflammation, and respiratory symptoms?

Researchers will compare inhaled tobramycin and oral ciprofloxacin in a randomized crossover design to determine whether participants with Pf phage-positive infection respond better to an antibiotic that is not predicted to be sequestered by Pf phage.

Participants will:

* Complete a 12-week randomized crossover study receiving both inhaled tobramycin and oral ciprofloxacin during separate treatment periods.
* Provide sputum samples for bacterial culture, bacterial density measurements, and inflammatory biomarker analyses.
* Provide blood samples for inflammatory biomarker analyses and safety monitoring
* Undergo pulmonary function testing, including spirometry for measurement of FEV1 and lung clearance index measurements.
* Complete quality-of-life assessments and undergo routine clinical and safety monitoring, including blood testing and anthropometric measurements.
primary_outcomes: Change in Forced Expiratory Volume in One Second (FEV1) following treatment With inhaled tobramycin versus oral ciprofloxacin
title: Pseudomonas & Pf Phage - Tobra vs Cipro

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of different irrigation needle designs on postoperative pain in mandibular first and second molars with pulp necrosis and no or mild preoperative pain.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does irrigation needle design influence the intensity of postoperative pain following root canal treatment? Are there differences in postoperative pain and analgesic consumption among open-ended, side-vented, and TruNatomy flexible plastic double side-vented irrigation needles?

Participants were randomly assigned to three groups:

Open-ended needle group: Root canal irrigation was performed using an open-ended irrigation needle.

Side-vented needle group: Root canal irrigation was performed using a side-vented irrigation needle.

TruNatomy group: Root canal irrigation was performed using a flexible plastic double side-vented TruNatomy irrigation needle.

All groups underwent standardized root canal treatment using the same instrumentation system, irrigation solutions, irrigation volumes, and obturation protocol. Postoperative pain was assessed at 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 72 hours, and analgesic consumption was recorded.
title: Effect of Irrigation Needle Design on Postoperative Pain

brief_summary:
Fine motor skill development is essential for academic readiness, functional independence, and school performance. Skills such as pincer grasp, hand dexterity, visual-motor integration, and cognitive processing support handwriting, while play-based activities provide engaging and developmentally appropriate ways to enhance these abilities. Although origami and play dough are commonly used, limited evidence compares their effectiveness.

This randomised clinical trial will compare the effects of origami and play dough on handwriting performance, cognition, hand dexterity, and visual-motor integration in 78 school-going children. Participants will be randomly allocated into origami and play dough groups. Pre and post-intervention assessments will use the ETCH-Manuscript Evaluation Tool, Box and Block Test, and Beery-Buktenica Developmental Test of Visual-Motor Integration. The six-week intervention will include three 25-minute supervised sessions per week, with activities progressing from simple to complex. Data will be analysed using SPSS version 27, with statistical significance set at p ≤ 0.05.
title: Comparative Effects of Origami on Hand Writing and Cognition

brief_summary:
Congenital varus equinus clubfoot (VECF) affects approximately 100,000 births per year worldwide and is estimated to occur in about 1 to 2 per 1,000 births in France. This malformation affects boys in two-thirds of cases and is bilateral in half of the cases. Its etiology and pathogenesis remain poorly understood.

During the 20th century, treatment was primarily surgical. This treatment was performed within the first year of life, but results deteriorated over time. This progression is characterized by muscle weakness, joint stiffness, and pain with intolerance to physical exertion. These symptoms impact quality of life after age 30, primarily due to degenerative changes, particularly in the hindfoot.

In 1948, the Ponseti method was developed and consists of several phases. First, a corrective phase involving 3 to 9 sets of lower-leg and foot casts made of plaster of Paris, applied every 5 to 7 days. Next, once the correction is satisfactory, a percutaneous tenotomy of the calcaneal tendon is performed to lengthen the triceps surae and thereby correct the residual equinus. This procedure is followed by the application of a new lower-leg and foot cast for 21 days. Finally, the consolidation phase begins after the deformity has been at least nearly completely corrected. This involves wearing splints 22 hours a day for 3 months, during naps and at night for 1 year, and finally at night until the child is 3-4 years old. This is therefore a minimally invasive, albeit restrictive, method that allows for a more physiological correction of clubfoot with equinus varus. It was not until the 21st century in France that this method became widespread and established itself as the standard of care for patients with clubfoot with equinus varus. However, there is a lack of literature regarding the long-term quality of life of patients treated using the Ponseti method.

At the same time, in the 1950s, the functional method was developed in France. This method involves treatment by massage therapists and physical therapists aimed at increasing the flexibility of patients' feet prior to corrective surgery. However, as the method's effectiveness became evident, surgery became less and less necessary for patients treated with the functional method. This method relies on manual mobilizations performed daily by physical therapists, combined with active stimulation of weak muscles, as well as the application of flexible splints made from Tensoplast®. This treatment for children with equinus varus clubfoot consists of three phases. First, the reduction phase, from birth to 6 weeks of age (7 sessions per week). Next, the refinement phase, from 6 weeks to 8 months (5 sessions per week). Finally, the pre-standing and standing phases, beginning at 8 months (3 or 4 sessions per week). The goal of the method is to restore normal tibiofibular function, achieve foot alignment, and reestablish a balanced motor pattern.

This is therefore a common condition in pediatric orthopedic surgery, yet there is a lack of data in the literature on long-term quality of life for patients treated with the Ponseti method and, subsequently, with the functional method - - . In this context, we therefore aim to assess the quality of life of these patients treated with these methods in the pediatric orthopedic surgery department at Angers University Hospital, with a focus on the Ponseti method.
title: Quality of Life and Outcomes at a Minimum of 10 Years for Patients With Varus Equinus Clubfoot Treated Using the Ponseti Method - QP10

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a dairy avoidance diet works to manage moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (eczema) in adults. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a dairy avoidance diet improve eczema control?
* Does a dairy avoidance diet improve eczema symptoms?
* Does a dairy avoidance diet improve quality of life?

Researchers will compare dairy avoidance diet to regular diet (participants will continue to consume their diet as usual) to see if a dairy avoidance diet works to manage moderate-to-severe eczema. Participants will:

* Eat a dairy avoidance diet or their regular diet every day for 16 weeks.
* Complete online surveys at the start of the study (baseline) and at weekly follow up for 16 weeks. Surveys will ask about the participant's health, well-being, and dairy intake.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Recap of Atopic Eczema (RECAP) score
title: Trial of Avoiding Dairy for Adult Atopic Dermatitis

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate whether genetic variants are associated with an inadequate response to carbamazepine and/or oxcarbazepine in patients with trigeminal neuralgia without neurovascular conflict.

This single-center, prospective observational cohort study will include 90 adult patients with trigeminal neuralgia in whom high-resolution MRI shows no neurovascular conflict, and who are starting treatment with carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine as part of routine clinical care. The study does not change patients' treatment.

Pain intensity will be assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) before treatment and after 1, 3 and 6 months. Inadequate treatment response is defined as a reduction in pain intensity of less than 50% after 6 months compared with baseline.

Genetic variants in the SCN9A, COMT, CYP3A4, CYP3A5 and HLA-A genes (including HLA-A\*31:01) will be analyzed from a blood sample. SCN9A is the primary gene of interest because it encodes the Nav1.7 sodium channel, the molecular target of carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Inadequate Treatment Response to Carbamazepine/Oxcarbazepine by SCN9A rs6746030 Genotype
title: Pharmacogenetic Predictors of Carbamazepine/Oxcarbazepine Response in Trigeminal Neuralgia Without Neurovascular Conflict

brief_summary: This is a multi-center, randomized, double-blind study evaluating the safety and efficacy of Neuviant™ multi-organ denervation (MDN), a combination drug-device therapy that uses the Neuviant Catheter to infuse dehydrated alcohol into the space surrounding the common hepatic and renal arteries to disrupt nearby sympathetic nerves. The denervation procedure is intended to be used along with medical therapy for lowering high blood sugar and high blood pressure in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hypertension (HTN) whose conditions remain inadequately controlled despite lifestyle modification and medications.

brief_summary:
The DRAGON-RA study is evaluating whether taking an oral vasodilator, calcium channel blocker or nitrate, once daily for 12 months after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery using a radial artery graft affects patient outcomes compared with taking no oral vasodilator for 12 months.

The study will compare outcomes between the groups, including the condition of the bypass grafts and clinical events, using study assessments and follow-up described in the protocol.

The study's hypothesis is that treatment with an oral vasodilator after CABG may improve radial artery graft outcomes compared with no oral vasodilator. The study will also assess the safety of the treatment and collect information about participants' health during follow-up.
lead_sponsor: Weill Medical College of Cornell University

brief_summary:
Basketball players often jump, sprint, stop suddenly and change direction during play. Good jumping ability and flexibility of the ankles and the back of the body are important for their performance. Many athletes use warm-up methods before training or games to prepare their bodies, and one of these methods is foam rolling. Foam rolling means the athlete rolls parts of their own body over a firm foam cylinder to apply pressure to the muscles and surrounding tissues.

Research shows that foam rolling can improve flexibility for a short time, but its effect on jumping is less clear. The results may depend on which body areas are rolled. In this study, foam rolling will focus on a connected line of tissues along the back of the body, called the Superficial Back Line. This line runs from the sole of the foot, along the back of the legs, to the back.

The purpose of this study is to compare a single session of foam rolling along this line with passive rest in male basketball players aged 14 to 18 years. The study will examine the immediate effects on three outcomes:

vertical jump performance ankle mobility (how far the ankle can bend upward) flexibility of the back of the body, measured with the sit-and-reach test The main question this study aims to answer is: Does foam rolling along the Superficial Back Line lead to different immediate changes in jumping performance, ankle mobility and posterior flexibility compared with passive rest?
title: Acute Effects of Foam Rolling on Jump Performance and Lower Limb Mobility in Adolescent Basketball Players

brief_summary:
The purpose of this prospective observational cohort study is to evaluate and compare the long-term clinical efficacy, painless sitting duration, and functional outcomes of two routinely performed interventional pain management procedures-Ganglion Impar Block (GIB) and Caudal Epidural Steroid Injection (CESI)-in patients with chronic coccydynia that has not responded to conservative treatments.

Chronic coccydynia (persistent tailbone pain) is a painful condition that significantly impairs daily functionality, particularly during sitting. When medications, ergonomic cushions, and physical therapy fail to provide adequate pain relief, interventional nerve blocks are commonly indicated in routine clinical practice. However, prospective comparative evidence regarding which technique provides superior long-term comfort, prolonged painless sitting, and functional recovery remains limited.

In this study, adult patients undergoing either GIB or CESI under fluoroscopic guidance as part of their routine care at the Algology Clinic will be prospectively observed. Patients will be evaluated before the procedure (baseline) and followed up at 1 hour, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-procedure. The primary objective is to determine the rate of meaningful clinical treatment success (defined as a 50% or greater reduction in pain) at 6 months, and to identify independent patient characteristics that predict long-term improvement.
primary_outcomes: Treatment Success Rate at 1, 3, and 6 Months Post-Procedure
title: Ganglion Impar Block Versus Caudal Epidural Steroid Injection in Chronic Coccydynia

brief_summary:
Breastfeeding is universally recognized as the most beneficial source of nutrition for newborns, providing essential nutrients and immunological protection during the early stages of life.

World Health Organization (WHO) recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life. However, many postpartum mothers face significant challenges in establishing and maintaining successful breastfeeding, with breast engorgement being one of the most common and distressing complications encountered in the early postpartum period. Breast engorgement is characterized by overfilling of the breast with milk, blood, and other fluids, resulting in swelling, pain, and difficulty in latching, which ultimately leads to early cessation of breastfeeding. If left unmanaged, engorgement can progress to mastitis, abscess formation, and complete abandonment of breastfeeding. Various non-pharmacological interventions have been proposed to manage breast engorgement and promote successful breastfeeding, among which Oketani Massage and Reverse Pressure Softening (RPS) are gaining increasing clinical attention. brief_summary:
Patients living with chronic lung diseases (CLD) are at high risk of frailty, malnutrition, and depression. However, many of the interventions targeting these conditions are underutilized. Thus, artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) offer a promising approach to guide targeted interventions for this population and reduce risk of hospitalization.

The purpose of this study is to assess the acceptability and feasibility of a new AI-CDSS for community-dwelling patients with CLD. The goal of this AI-CDSS is to predict the probability that patients would benefit from 5 frailty- and depression-focused interventions (pulmonary rehabilitation, physical therapy, fall-risk assessment, nutrition consultation, and depression consultation).

In this study, pulmonologists will review the AI-CDSS's predictions and have the option to recommend referrals for their patients. If a referral is recommended, the study team will contact the patient to discuss the referral and start the referral process. All participants will then complete a semi-structured interview and feedback survey asking their opinions about the AI-CDSS and the study referral process.
interventions: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support tool for recommending referrals for chronic lung disease patients

brief_summary:
Repeated implantation failure (RIF) occurs when pregnancy is not achieved despite repeated transfers of good-quality embryos during in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment. Although embryo quality is an important factor affecting implantation, abnormalities or subtle variations in uterine anatomy may also contribute to unsuccessful implantation.

Three-dimensional transvaginal ultrasound (3D-TVUS) allows detailed assessment of the shape and structure of the uterus, including the uterine cavity, fundal contour, wall thicknesses, and anatomical angles. Recently published research has established reference values for these measurements in women with normal uterine anatomy. However, it remains unclear whether women with repeated implantation failure demonstrate subtle uterine morphological differences that fall outside these reference ranges.

The aim of this prospective, single-center observational pilot study is to characterize three-dimensional uterine morphology in women with repeated implantation failure and compare their measurements with published normative reference values.

The study will include 50 women aged 18-34 years with repeated implantation failure following IVF or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) treatment.

Participants will undergo routine two-dimensional and three-dimensional transvaginal ultrasound during the proliferative phase of the menstrual cycle. Standardized measurements of uterine dimensions, fundal indentation, cavity configuration, myometrial wall thicknesses, and uterine angles will be obtained.

The primary objective is to characterize the distribution of these uterine measurements and compare them with published normative reference values from the Normal Uterus Assessment (NURSE) study.

Secondary objectives include determining the proportion of participants with measurements outside established normative percentile ranges and exploring possible associations between uterine morphology and the number of unsuccessful embryo transfers.

No experimental treatment or additional research-assigned intervention will be performed. The study findings may help identify previously unrecognized uterine morphological characteristics associated with repeated implantation failure and provide preliminary data for future larger studies.
primary_outcomes: Three-Dimensional Uterine Morphometric Measurements Compared With Published Normative Reference Values
title: Three-Dimensional Uterine Morphology in Women With Repeated Implantation Failure

brief_summary:
Moyamoya disease is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by narrowing or occlusion of major intracranial arteries and the development of abnormal collateral vessels. Surgical revascularization is an important treatment for patients with ischemic moyamoya disease. However, cerebral infarction and other neurological complications may occur during the perioperative period.

Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a noninvasive procedure involving repeated, brief periods of blood flow restriction and restoration in the limbs. It may improve the brain's tolerance to ischemic injury.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether RIPC can reduce the risk of cerebral infarction and neurological complications following revascularization surgery in patients with ischemic moyamoya disease.

This study is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial involving 230 participants. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive either RIPC or sham RIPC in addition to standard surgical treatment and perioperative care.

The primary outcomes are the incidence of new cerebral infarction within 7 days after surgery and the incidence of neurological complications within 30 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes include neurological function, perioperative complications, and intervention-related adverse events.

The findings may provide clinical evidence for a simple, noninvasive approach to improving perioperative outcomes in patients with moyamoya disease.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of New Cerebral Infarction Within 7 Days After Surgery
Incidence of Neurological Complications Within 30 Days After Surgery

brief_summary: This study builds upon the overarching hypothesis of the FAMILIA studies: early and repeated exposure to structured cardiovascular health promotion programs can shape long-term behavior and reduce lifetime cardiovascular risk. FAMILIA Cardiovascular Chobani Health Program specifically targets adolescents, evaluating whether a 4-month after-school intervention can act as a behavioral booster for those previously exposed to health promotion in early childhood, while also evaluating its impact in adolescents with no prior exposure. A secondary objective is to assess the sustainability of changes in mindset and behavior, while also assessing whether physiological health factors change over a two-year follow-up period. To complement the adolescent's findings, the study includes a parallel assessment of progression of subclinical atherosclerosis in parents who received a similar intervention a decade earlier as part of FAMILIA Project I. In FAMILIA Project I, prevalence of subclinical atherosclerosis was evaluated by vascular ultrasound and its associations with sociodemographic factors have been already published. Subclinical atherosclerosis in parents serves as a marker of long-term cardiovascular risk, offering insight into how risk may accumulate over time and potentially mirror future trajectories in their children.

brief_summary:
Stroke is a primary cause of long term disability frequently resulting in upper limb motor impairment that is both widespread and lasting. Improving independence and quality of life for stroke survivors hinges on the crucial recovery of arm and hand function. Traditional rehabilitation often relies on single prolonged therapy sessions which may limit the total effective dose and contribute to fatigue. Present research suggests that distributed or micro dose practice delivered in multiple short sessions throughout the day may enhance motor learning and neuroplasticity. Additionally, telerehabilitation has emerged as a feasible way to provide therapy remotely increasing accessibility and adherence. Despite these advancements there is bounded evidence comparing micro dose distributed practice with conventional single session therapy for upper limb recovery highlighting a gap in optimal therapy scheduling strategies. The aim of study is to compare the effects of micro dose task practice delivered throughout the day via telerehabilitation versus conventional single session therapy on upper limb motor recovery in stroke survivors.

This study will be a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of 12 weeks. Sampling technique will be non- probability convenient that will include stroke survivors aged 45-65 years with upper limb motor deficits, medically stable and able to follow commands. To identify relevant participants a comprehensive screening approach will be adopted selecting adult stroke survivors with upper limb impairment and excluding those with severe cognitive or medical limitations. Participants will then be randomly allocated into two groups to reduce allocation bias. The intervention for the experimental group will comprise multiple 4 short practice sessions of 12 minutes distributed throughout the day delivered via a telerehabilitation platform embracing principles of task oriented and repetitive training, which have been shown to support upper limb motor recovery in systematic rehabilitation research. The control group

will receive a single 50 minutes continuous therapy session per day in a clinical setting consistent with conventional therapy schedules used in comparative rehabilitation studies. Improvement or recovery of upper limb will be assessed by using Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) and Action Research Arm Test (ARAT). Further health-related quality of life will be measured by using Stroke-Specific Quality of Life Scale (SS-QOL). Pre-, mid intervention at 6 week and post-intervention outcomes will be analyzed using paired and independent t-tests or appropriate non-parametric tests. Effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals will be calculated to determine clinical significance.
title: Effects of Micro Dose Task Practice Via Telerehabilitation Vs Conventional Therapy on Upper Limb Function After Stroke

brief_summary:
Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide. Most commonly, lower limb impairments, including plantarflexor and dorsiflexor spasticity, reduce range of motion, impair proprioception, and affect muscle strength. Such impairment leads to reduced balance, abnormal gait, reduced functional mobility, and effects on the quality of life of individuals with stroke. Dry needling (DN) is an invasive technique for reducing spasticity, decreasing muscle tone, reducing myofascial trigger points, improving blood circulation, and improving muscle extensibility. Eccentric exercise plays a key role in improving muscle strength and control, enhancing muscle lengthening, and improving functional performance. To evaluate the effects of dry needling combined with eccentric exercise on spasticity and lower limb function in individuals with stroke. And compare changes in spasticity, strength, gait, and functional mobility between the two groups.

The study will be conducted as a randomized clinical trial with two groups. The sample size will be 36, with 18 participants in each group. Participants will have a stroke. Group A will receive a deep dry needling technique combined with eccentric exercise, and group B will receive sham dry needling combined with eccentric exercise. Primary outcomes will be spasticity, strength, functional mobility and gait. The study will collect data at baseline, after four week and after eight week using validated outcome measures: The Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) for spasticity, Manual Muscle Testing (MMT) for muscle strength, Fugl Meyer Assessment lower Extremity (FMA-LE) for functional mobility, and 10-Meter walk test (10-MWT) for gait speed. There will be three dry needling sessions in a week for four weeks and three sessions of eccentric exercise for eight weeks. The data will be analyzed using appropriate statistical methods and measured by using SPSS software version 27. This study's results can provide valuable information to healthcare professionals and may contribute to the development of future research in this area.
interventions: Dry Needling combined with Eccentric exercise
Sham Dry Needling Combined with Eccentric Exercise
title: Effects of Dry Needling Combined With Eccentric Exercise in Individuals With Stroke.

brief_summary:
Interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of pulmonary disorders characterized by interstitial inflammation, fibrosis, or both. Acute exacerbations of ILD (AE-ILD), characterized by acute respiratory deterioration, represent a major cause of hospitalization and mortality. Although initially recognized in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), acute exacerbations can also occur in other forms of ILD, including connective tissue disease-associated ILD, fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis, unclassifiable ILD, and other progressive fibrotic ILDs. AE-ILD is associated with a substantially increased risk of short-term mortality.

This study is a single-center cohort study comprising both retrospective and prospective components. This real-world observational study will enroll patients with stable ILD attending outpatient clinics and patients hospitalized with AE-ILD. Patients with stable ILD will be followed to investigate the incidence and risk factors of acute exacerbations and to develop a risk prediction model. Patients hospitalized with AE-ILD will undergo systematic evaluation of clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, imaging features, infection-related factors, treatments, and clinical outcomes to identify prognostic factors and develop prognostic prediction models. In addition, diagnostic models for AE-ILD will be explored using relevant clinical, imaging, and biomarker data, with appropriate comparison groups.

A standardized ILD biobank will be established to facilitate future investigations into the biological mechanisms, diagnostic biomarkers, and prognostic indicators of AE-ILD.

The findings are expected to improve risk stratification, facilitate early recognition of acute exacerbations, and provide evidence to optimize clinical management and follow-up strategies for patients with ILD.

standard postoperative rehabilitation alone standard rehabilitation plus EMG-BF-assisted functional task training targeting the abductor pollicis brevis (APB) standard rehabilitation plus mirror therapy-assisted functional task training

All groups will receive treatment 3 days per week for 8 weeks. A blinded assessor will evaluate symptom severity, hand function, pain, grip and pinch strength, manual dexterity, sensation, wrist proprioception, forearm muscle activation and motor dual-task performance before and after the 8-week program.

brief_summary:
This multicenter interventional clinical study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of personalized photodynamic therapy (PDT) using the CerCa System® for the treatment of high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2 and CIN 3) in women aged 18 to 60 years.

The study is conducted at two clinical centers in Sao Paulo State, Brazil: the Women's Health Outpatient Clinic in Araraquara and the University Hospital of the Federal University of Sao Carlos (HU-UFSCar).

Eligible participants must have histologically confirmed CIN 2 or CIN 3, with a single, fully visible cervical lesion located outside the squamocolumnar junction, without extension into the endocervical canal.

Participants are divided into two age groups: Group 1 includes women aged 18 to 24 years, and Group 2 includes women aged 25 to 60 years. Both groups receive PDT using topical methyl aminolevulinate (MAL) and red light delivered by the CerCa System®.

All participants initially receive two PDT sessions separated by 21 days. Depending on clinical and laboratory response, up to two additional sessions may be administered.

Participants aged 18 to 24 years undergo clinical and laboratory follow-up without routinely scheduled cervical excisional surgery, with additional diagnostic procedures or conventional treatment when clinically indicated. Participants aged 25 to 60 years may undergo loop electrosurgical excision (LEEP) according to the study protocol and treatment response.

Treatment effectiveness is assessed through colposcopic and cytological findings, changes in HPV DNA signal measured by hybrid capture assay, and HPV DNA detection by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Histopathological regression and immunohistochemical expression of p16 and Ki-67 are evaluated when cervical tissue specimens are available. Treatment-related adverse events are also monitored.

Participants are followed for up to 24 months to assess treatment response, lesion persistence or recurrence, and safety. The study aims to investigate PDT as a potential less invasive treatment approach for women with high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia.
primary_outcomes: Histopathological Regression of High-Grade Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia
Percentage of Participants With Undetectable HPV DNA by PCR After Photodynamic Therapy

brief_summary:
This mixed-methods study evaluates the implementation of videolaryngoscopy for airway management during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in an emergency medical services (EMS) organisation in western Sweden.

The study consists of two components. First, a pre-post implementation study compares adult patients with OHCA managed before and after the introduction of videolaryngoscopy. The historical control group includes patients managed before implementation, while the intervention group includes patients managed after all ambulances had been equipped with a SecMAC+ videolaryngoscope and EMS personnel had completed training in its use. Eligible patients are adults with OHCA in whom cardiopulmonary resuscitation is performed by EMS and an airway management intervention is used to establish a patent airway and enable ventilation. The study focuses on patients with an initial rhythm of asystole or pulseless electrical activity.

The primary outcome is successful endotracheal intubation (ETI) performed by the EMS crew during the OHCA event. Additional outcomes include the proportion of patients receiving ETI, number of intubation attempts, airway management interventions, and return of spontaneous circulation.

Second, EMS personnel responsible for airway management in the intervention group complete a survey assessing their experience of using videolaryngoscopy during OHCA, including perceived ease of use and visualization of the vocal cords during intubation.

The study aims to determine whether implementation of videolaryngoscopy is associated with an increased proportion of patients receiving ETI and to describe EMS personnel's experiences of videolaryngoscopy in the prehospital cardiac arrest setting.

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to learn whether a student-centered Complementary Training Program (CTP) can reduce disruptive behaviors in secondary school physical education (PE) lessons. It also looks at whether the program makes lessons run more smoothly and improves students' attention. The study included 1164 Grade 8 students (about 13 years old) in 40 classes from two public schools in Tunisia. The main questions it aims to answer are: (1) Does the CTP reduce the number of disruptive behaviors (distraction, impulsivity, disturbing behavior, provocative behavior) observed during PE lessons over one school year? (2) Does the CTP reduce lesson interruptions (fractures) and increase the share of incidents handled without stopping the activity? (3) Does the CTP increase the share of disruptive behaviors that students stop on their own within 30 seconds? (4) Does the CTP improve attentional performance on the d2 Test of Attention? Researchers compared classes that received the CTP (20 classes) with classes that followed the regular PE curriculum only (20 classes). Students in the CTP group took part in 40 hours of training during the 2023-2024 school year: 16 hours of theory (five modules on recognizing disruptive behaviors and their effect on the lesson) and 24 hours of practical team-sport sessions (five interventions with feedback, rotating roles, and video self-review). One PE lesson per class was video-recorded at the start (September), middle (January), and end (May) of the school year, and students completed the d2 Test of Attention at the same three time points.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out if people with depression can be helped with their symptoms by going through a mystical experience paired with psychotherapy (sometimes called talk therapy). Mystical experiences are profound and highly meaningful states of consciousness in which people report a sense of unity or "oneness" with everything, highly positive emotions, and a sense of having something important revealed to them. Previous research suggests that patients with depression can experience improvement in their symptoms after having a mystical experience while under the influence of a psychedelic substance (e.g., psilocybin, ayahuasca). This study seeks to answer if a mystical experience brought about through hypnosis can also have a positive effect on symptoms of depression.

Participants will participate in seven sessions of psychotherapy and respond to questionnaires of various lengths at five time points. All study visits that involve meeting with a psychotherapist will occur in the laboratory facility in which the baseline session occurs. In chronological order, these involve:

* Eligibility screening: Completion of an online survey to confirm eligibility to participate in study (already completed): 15-20 minutes
* Baseline appointment: Meeting with study personnel prior to first session of psychotherapy to confirm intention to participate in study, complete 12 short questionnaires, and schedule first session, 60-90 minutes
* Preparation sessions (2): Meet with psychotherapist to discuss symptoms, current stressors, and goals for treatment, 60 minutes (x2)
* Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience (GIME) sessions (2): Meet with psychotherapist for a hypnosis session for mystical experience, 60-75 minutes (x2)
* Post-GIME assessment (2): Complete two brief questionnaires immediately following each GIME session, 10-15 minutes (x2)
* Integration sessions (3): Meet with psychotherapist to discuss experience(s) during GIME sessions and integrate insights into daily life, 60 minutes (x2), 30 minutes (x1)
* Audio recordings: Participants will be asked to listen to a brief, relaxation-based audio recording at home approximately 3x per week following the first GIME session.
* Endpoint assessment: Participants complete 13 brief computer-based questionnaires (20-35 minutes), participate in a brief assessment to gauge hypnotic ability (10-15 minutes), and (optional) participate in a brief interview (10-20 minutes), total 50-70 minutes. An audio/video recording of participants will be made if they elect to participate in the optional, brief interview.
* Follow up assessment: Complete 7 brief computer-based questionnaires, 15-25 minutes
interventions: Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience (GIME) with Integration
primary_outcomes: Number of participants who complete treatment
Number of participants who complete study measures
title: Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience (GIME) for the Treatment of Unipolar Depression Among Adults: A Feasibility Study
