brief_summary:
Short stature is one of the most common reasons for consultation in pediatric endocrinology, defined as a height below -2 standard deviations (SD) of the mean for healthy children of the same sex and age. Its etiology is complex: it may represent a normal physiological variant, but it is frequently associated with various endocrine disorders, chromosomal abnormalities, impaired intrauterine growth, or chronic diseases. Among these, growth hormone deficiency (GHD), idiopathic short stature (ISS), small for gestational age (SGA), Turner syndrome (TS), and Noonan syndrome (NS) are the five most common types of short stature currently treatable with growth hormone in clinical practice.

Inpegsomatropin Injection is a domestically developed long-acting growth hormone that has been approved for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (PGHD). In a completed confirmatory clinical study of this product, a multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial compared Inpegsomatropin Injection (once weekly) with recombinant human growth hormone (Norditropin®, once daily) in treatment-naïve prepubertal patients with PGHD. The results showed that Inpegsomatropin Injection at 0.14 mg/kg/week effectively improved height velocity (HV) in PGHD patients, with efficacy comparable to Norditropin® at 245 μg/kg/week, and a favorable overall safety profile similar to that of short-acting growth hormone. In a multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled phase II basket study of this product, treatment-naïve prepubertal children with ISS, SGA, or TS were enrolled. The results showed that Inpegsomatropin Injection at 280 μg/kg/week for 52 weeks had no significant drug accumulation, with efficacy and safety comparable to once-daily recombinant human growth hormone (Norditropin®) at 470 μg/kg/week. However, data on the long-term safety of this product in children with various types of short stature remain limited.

This study plans to enroll children with short stature, covering the five common disease types-GHD, ISS, SGA, TS, and NS-using a multicenter, prospective cohort design to systematically evaluate the long-term safety of Inpegsomatropin Injection. It aims to provide evidence-based support for individualized clinical dosing, long-term treatment benefit assessment, and risk evaluation.
title: A Study of the Long-term Safety of Inpegsomatropin Injection in Children With Short Stature

brief_summary:
Mental disorders constitute a major challenge to both society, patients and science. Serious mental illnesses (SMIs), such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression and personality disorders, comprise some of the largest disease burdens worldwide, with no evidence of reduction in recent decades. A range of psycho-social and pharmacological interventions have demonstrated efficacy for improving symptomatic and functional outcomes of SMIs albeit with modest effect sizes and the development of novel, more effective treatments has largely stalled despite a significant number of patients will not respond to treatments. Additionally, there are substantial shortages in access to treatments as well as various barriers, such as perceived need for care and stigma surrounding mental health problems. The planned study aimed to develop and evaluate a novel modular, transdiagnostic psychotherapeutic intervention in n=130 youths at-risk for SMIs. The planned randomized controlled study compares the new developed intervention to TAU in five different study centres.

The Objective is to evaluate the modular, transdiagnostic CBT (AIM-Youth) approach for youths at-risk for SMIs compared to treatment as usual (TAU). Measurements take place as baseline, mid-treatment (3 month), post-treatment (6 month) and follow-up (12-48 month). The primary outcome measure will be psychological distress as measured by the CORE-10 at the end of treatment, secondary outcomes will be CHR-symptoms, quality of life, functioning as well as use of mental health resources at post and follow-up assessment.
title: Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial of a Transdiagnostic, Modular Intervention for Youth at Risk for Psychotic, Bipolar, or Borderline Personality Disorders

brief_summary:
This study investigated the effects of open-kinetic-chain (OKC) and closed-kinetic-chain (CKC) resistance training on elbow movement characteristics and muscle mechanical properties in strength-trained athletes.

The study used a randomized, parallel-group design. A total of 23 participants were assigned to either an OKC training group (n = 12) or a CKC training group (n = 11). Both groups completed an eight-week resistance training program involving three training sessions per week.

Muscle mechanical properties of the biceps brachii and triceps brachii were assessed using MyotonPRO, while elbow movement characteristics were evaluated using inertial measurement units (IMUs).

The study aimed to compare changes in muscle stiffness, muscle tone, mechanical decrement, elbow range of motion, angular velocity, movement duration, and movement variability between the two training approaches.

The findings were intended to improve understanding of how different resistance training approaches influence muscle mechanical behavior and the organization of elbow movements.
primary_outcomes: Change in Muscle Stiffness of the Biceps Brachii and Triceps Brachii
title: Effects of Open- Versus Closed-Kinetic-Chain Resistance Training on Elbow Movement and Muscle Mechanics in Strength Athletes

brief_summary: The study will use a quasi-experimental design conducted over ten months in thalassemia department of tertiary care hospital. It will include 24 children aged 8-12 years , selected after eligibility screening and guardian consent. Outcomes will be assessed using Six-Minute Walk Test for functional capacity and aerobic capacity,, Pulse Oximeter for heart rate and SpO2 measurement, Pediatric quality of life inventory-multidimensional fatigue scale (PedsQL-MFS) to measure symptoms of fatigue. Ethical approval will be obtained from the Research Ethical Committee of Riphah International University, Lahore, and data will be analyzed using SPSS version 26.0
primary_outcomes: Pediatric quality of life inventory-multidimensional fatigue scale (PedsQL-MFS)
title: Effects of Pin Wheel Therapy on Cardiorespiratory Parameters and Fatigue in Children With Thalassemia

brief_summary:
Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic progressive autoimmune synovial-mediated disease. A considerable proportion of patients with difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA), especially persistent inflammatory refractory rheumatoid arthritis (PIRRA), cannot achieve disease remission after conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) and multiple lines of biologic or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (tsDMARD). New therapeutic strategies are urgently needed for these patients.

Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of etanercept combined with tofacitinib in patients with persistent inflammatory refractory rheumatoid arthritis (PIRRA).

Study design: Multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial. Patients diagnosed with persistent inflammatory refractory rheumatoid arthritis (PIRRA) will be enrolled and randomized to receive combination therapy of etanercept plus tofacitinib versus standard-of-care treatment.

Conclusions: This trial aims to explore whether combined therapy of tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) and Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi) can improve remission rate for PIRRA patients, and provide evidence for optimized therapeutic strategy for difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA).
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Inner Mongolia Medical University
title: Etanercept Combined With Tofacitinib for the Treatment of Persistent Inflammatory Refractory Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary: Urdu-speaking children with DS present a language profile marked by relatively preserved transitive/intransitive verb use and high-cue-validity grammatical morphology (tense, causative) alongside disproportionate difficulty with negation, compounded by persistent, atypical phonological error patterns.
title: Verb and Morpheme Production in Urdu-Speaking Children With Down Syndrome: A Morphosyntactic Profile

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to assess the impact of the Helping Men Recover (HMR) curriculum at California State Prison-Corcoran. The HMR program to be evaluated utilizes a Peer-Facilitated model of implementation (i.e., residents serving life or long sentences will be trained to facilitate the delivery of the HMR program to other residents). The peer-facilitated program is delivered over 21 sessions and utilizes a Facilitator Guide and Participant Workbook. This evaluation study will employ a randomized experimental design; the most rigorous design that can be employed in evaluation research.

The program is delivered by trained peer facilitators in general institutional housing on a custody level III yard. Researchers assess changes in trauma-related distress, behavioral health symptoms, anger, and aggression using validated self-report measures administered before and after the intervention period.
interventions: Helping Men Recover: A Program for Treating Addiction 2nd Edition Covington, S., Griffin, D., and Dauer, R. (2022). Hoboken, NJ: Wiley
primary_outcomes: Modified Short Screening Scale for DSM-IV PTSD (7-item symptom index, following a trauma-exposure screen)
title: Helping Men Recover

brief_summary: This study investigates the effects of the traditional string game Cat's Cradle on handwriting skills, finger dexterity, and bilateral hand coordination in 56 school-going children aged 8-12 years at Mutahir Public School, Ghakhar Mandi. Participants will be randomly divided into an experimental group and a control group of 28 children each. The experimental group will perform structured Cat's Cradle and free-play activities, while the control group will participate in free play only, for 20-30 minutes, 3-4 times weekly, over 4-6 weeks. Pre- and post-intervention assessments will be conducted using standardized tools, and data will be analyzed using SPSS to determine the effectiveness of Cat's Cradle in improving handwriting-related motor skills.
title: Effects of Cats Cradle on Hand Writing Skills and Bilateral Hand Coordination Among School Going Children

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial is designed to evalute Beyond Trauma (BT). Beyond Trauma promotes a strength-based approach that seeks to empower women and increase their sense of self. The exercises are designed to give them a corrective experience of connecting with others in a safe environment. In using this model, the facilitator helps the women in the group to see the strengths they have and to increase the skills they need. The curriculum also focuses on emotional development. Dealing with the expression and containment of feelings (fear, loss, grief, anger, shame) is a critical part of trauma work. The program uses cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT), expressive arts, body-oriented strategies, and is based on the principles of relational therapy. In addition, there is a segment on specific issues in the criminal justice settings, and the end of each of the 12 sessions has information on adapting for girls. The study is being conducted at a California correctional facility and compares participants randomly assigned to BT with participants assigned to a waitlist control condition. The program is delivered by trained peer facilitators in general institutional housing. Researchers are assessing changes in trauma-related distress and behavioral health symptoms using validated self-report measures administered before and after the intervention period. The study examines between-group differences in post-traumatic stress symptoms, global trauma symptoms, anxiety, depression, dissociation, sexual abuse-related trauma symptoms, and sleep disturbances.
interventions: Beyond Trauma: A Healing Journey for Women
primary_outcomes: Modified Short Screening Scale for DSM-IV PTSD (7-item symptom index, following a trauma-exposure screen)
title: Beyond Trauma (BT): A Healing Journey for Women

brief_summary: We will conduct a prospective, randomized trial of 602 adults who smoke in the rural Midwest. Participants will be randomized to either: (Control) mailed computer/internet access resources, or (Intervention) computer/internet access resources plus the COACH intervention.
primary_outcomes: Self-reported 7-day smoking abstinence at 4, 12, and 26 weeks post-randomization
title: Digital Literacy Coaching to Support Smoking Cessation in Rural Communities: Increasing Digital Engagement and Access

brief_summary:
1. Study Background

   The "Healthy China 2030" Planning Outline explicitly states that the focus of medical work should shift from treatment to prevention. Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is associated with poor quality of life, rapid decline in lung function, and increased mortality \[1\]. It is a major cause of morbidity, disability, and mortality worldwide. Most Chinese COPD patients are at a high risk of exacerbation, with an average of two exacerbation events per year. The prevalence of COPD in China is 8.6% among adults aged over 20, 13.7% among those over 40, and over 27% among those over 60, with an estimated total of approximately 99.9 million patients nationwide.

   Current research and clinicians primarily focus on the treatment of AECOPD. However, the prevention and prediction of AECOPD are key to improving clinical treatment levels, patient quality of life, and achieving a good prognosis. Accurate prediction and early detection of acute exacerbations will facilitate early treatment and reduce mortality \[1\]. The Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) 2023 report and top journals, including The Lancet, have commented that accurate risk assessment of COPD exacerbations is of great significance for treatment selection and is crucial for understanding disease burden and predicting future healthcare utilization trends.

   Currently, there is no exact and complete consensus on the transition mechanism from COPD to AECOPD, and there is a lack of objective evaluation criteria. Existing evaluations are mainly based on clinical symptoms and/or pulmonary function test data, which are susceptible to subjective factors such as patient tolerance, cooperation, and evaluator experience. There is an urgent clinical need for an objective, safe, and efficient method for AECOPD risk assessment and prediction to carry out precise and personalized evaluation and treatment. Therefore, further integrating broader information to early identify respiratory abnormalities, understand the potential pathological mechanisms of the dynamic transition from COPD to AECOPD, and explore clinical markers has important social value and clinical significance.
2. Study Objective

   To establish a prediction model for the transition from COPD to AECOPD based on dynamic radiomics predictors from chest CT images and clinical factors.
3. Trial Design

3.1 Total Sample Size This study retrospectively collected clinical information, chest CT imaging, and laboratory data of 200 COPD patients admitted to our hospital from January 2020 to December 2024.

3.2 Patient Selection Criteria 3.2.1 Inclusion Criteria

1. Age \> 18 years;
2. Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of COPD based on clinical data and imaging examinations, meeting the GOLD diagnostic criteria.

3.2.2 Exclusion Criteria

1. Age ≤ 18 years;
2. Missing data;
3. Poor image quality.

3.3 Clinical and Radiological Data Collection

Patient Follow-up and Grouping:

Enrolled patients were followed up by telephone and divided into a stable group and an AECOPD risk group based on whether AECOPD occurred.

Data Collection:

Baseline chest CT images and clinical indicators at enrollment were collected for the enrolled COPD patients. Chest CT scans were performed using multi-slice spiral CT volume scanning. The scanning parameters were as follows: tube voltage 120 kV, tube current (automatic mA), collimation 128 × 0.625 mm, pitch 1, acquisition slice thickness 5 mm, and image reconstruction slice thickness 0.625 mm. Before scanning, subjects were instructed to practice breath-holding at the end of deep inspiration. Scanning method: Subjects were placed in a supine position with hands clasped behind the head, without contrast agent injection, and scanned at the end of deep inspiration from the lung apex to the lung base. The obtained images were transferred to a GE AW4.7 workstation, and the required CT images were obtained using the standard (Stnd) reconstruction algorithm.

Clinical indicators included: laboratory indicators (blood routine, CRP, PCT, BEC, D-dimer, serum sodium, BNP, etc.), clinical symptom indicators (respiratory rate), and pulmonary function indicators (forced vital capacity \[FVC\], forced expiratory volume in 1 second \[FEV1\], FEV1/FVC ratio, peak expiratory flow \[PEF\], peak inspiratory flow \[PIF\], maximum expiratory pressure \[MEP\], maximum inspiratory pressure \[MIP\], maximal mid-expiratory flow \[MMEF\], maximal voluntary ventilation \[MVV\]). (Note: CPR, PTC were corrected to CRP, PCT for clinical accuracy) 4. Study Procedures

4.1 Screening According to the screening criteria in Section 3.2, patient data were collected through the hospital's Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) and Electronic Medical Record System (EMRS).

4.2 Data Organization

The following information was collected for all cases:

1. Clinical information: gender, age;
2. Chest CT radiological information.

4.3 Statistical Analysis and Model
primary_outcomes: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of the COPD-to-AECOPD Prediction Model
title: Diagnostic Accuracy Study of a Chest X-ray Based Radiomics Model for Identifying Early Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

brief_summary:
Many patients develop or suffer worsening of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) and need long-term acid suppression. Vonoprazan, a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), suppresses gastric acid faster and for longer than proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and is taken once daily.

This randomized trial compares vonoprazan 20 mg once daily with pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily in adults with reflux symptoms at least 3 months after LSG. The main question is which drug gives the greater improvement in reflux symptoms and reflux-related quality of life, measured with the GERD Health-Related Quality of Life (GERD-HRQL) questionnaire. Patient satisfaction, side effects and the need to escalate or change treatment will also be compared.
title: Vonoprazan Versus Pantoprazole for Reflux Symptoms After Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy

brief_summary:
Background: Epicardial atherosclerotic obstruction alone does not fully explain ischemic syndromes such as INOCA, ANOCA, and MINOCA. Coronary microvascular disease (CMD) is now recognized as a major pathophysiological and prognostic determinant of coronary artery disease, driven by periarteriolar fibrosis, medial-intimal hypertrophy, microembolization, and endothelial dysfunction, and is associated with angina, non-fatal myocardial infarction, hospitalization, and cardiovascular death. In acute coronary syndromes, thrombosis and microembolization further contribute to slow-flow/no-reflow during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). No validated therapy currently reverses microvascular dysfunction. Papaverine, an opium-derived vasodilator used to treat slow-flow/no-reflow and to induce hyperemia for fractional flow reserve (FFR) assessment, inhibits cAMP- and cGMP-specific phosphodiesterases. This trial evaluates whether intracoronary papaverine, by reducing microvascular resistance, can limit infarct size and ischemic injury after acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

Objectives: Primary-to assess improvement in angiography-derived microvascular resistance (MR), measured by quantitative flow ratio (QFR), following intracoronary papaverine verphosphodiesterases. This trial evaluates whether intracoronary papaverine, by reducing microvascular resistance, can limit infarct size and ischemic injury after acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

Objectives: Primary-to assess improvement in angiography-derived microvascular resistance (MR), measured by quantitative flow ratio (QFR), following intracoronary papaverine versus placebo. Secondary-to evaluate infarct size, microvascular obstruction, regional wall-motion abnormalities, and left ventricular ejection fraction by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR); TIMI flow grade; troponin and BNP kinetics; and safety outcomes, including hypotension, cardiogenic shock, arrhythmias, stroke, and death.

Methods: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at Instituto do Coração (HCFMUSP) and Hospital Agamenon Magalhães. Adults with AMI (Killip class I-II) undergoing successful culprit-lesion PCI will be randomized 1:1 using REDCap to receive intracoronary papaverine (20 mg/2 mL) or saline placebo. Study medication will be prepared and administered in a blinded fashion. Microvascular resistance will be calculated using QFR at three time points (pre-infusion, post-PCI, and post-medication), while infarct characteristics will be assessed by CMR using T1, T2, and T2\* mapping. The primary outcome will be analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusted for baseline angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AngioMR) measured after primary PCI.

Sample size was calculated based on the population standard deviation of AngioMR in patients with STEMI and was powered to detect a treatment effect corresponding to at least 60% of the microvascular obstruction gradient identified by CMR. Assuming 90% power, a two-sided significance level of 0.05, and an estimated 15% loss to follow-up, the minimum required sample size was 35 patients per group (70 total). To enhance the robustness of efficacy and safety analyses in the setting of acute coronary syndrome, the final planned sample size is 100 patients (50 per group).

Under the assumptions used for the sample size calculation, the two groups are expected to differ as follows. In the saline (control) group, the average AMR is expected to be approximately 26.4 mmHg·s/dm. This value is derived from the median AMR of patients with STEMI treated with primary PCI in the reference cohort and therefore represents the expected value in the absence of vasodilator administration. In the papaverine group, the average AMR is expected to be approximately 23.4 mmHg·s/dm. This value corresponds to the control value minus the treatment effect of 3.0 mmHg·s/dm that the study is designed to detect. These values represent the treatment difference for which the study is powered and do not constitute a previously demonstrated effect of papaverine. The selected treatment effect is also considered clinically meaningful: an AMR of approximately 23.4 mmHg·s/dm falls below the high-risk threshold of approximately 25-27 mmHg·s/dm reported in independent STEMI cohorts, whereas the control value of 26.4 mmHg·s/dm remains within that high-risk range. Thus, the treatment effect under investigation would correspond to a shift in the average patient from the high-risk range toward the preserved range.

Timeline: Fifteen months (6 months for recruitment, 6 months for data analysis, and 3 months for manuscript preparation).

Significance: By evaluating a low-cost, ANVISA-approved agent, the PAP-MICRO TRIAL may provide the first randomized evidence supporting a pharmacological strategy specifically targeting coronary microvascular dysfunction in AMI, with the potential to reduce infarct size and improve cardiovascular outcomes.
lead_sponsor: University of Sao Paulo General Hospital
primary_outcomes: Angiography-Derived Microvascular Resistance (AMR) Measured by Quantitative Flow Ratio
title: Effects of Papaverine on Microvascular Resistance in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

brief_summary: This prospective single-arm study will evaluate the implementation and effectiveness of a structured supervised exercise program for men with prostate cancer receiving carbon ion radiotherapy.
title: Supervised Exercise Program During Carbon Ion Radiotherapy for Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
The purpose of this intervention study is to examine the impact of environmental literacy training provided to university students on their awareness of global climate change, ecological footprint, and a sustainable environment. Additionally, the study aims to gather information regarding the students' levels of environmental literacy. The core questions it seeks to answer are:

Does environmental literacy training influence awareness of global climate change? Does environmental literacy training reduce one's ecological footprint? Does environmental literacy training increase awareness of a sustainable environment? To determine the effectiveness of the environmental literacy training, the researchers will compare experimental and control groups.

Participants will:

Receive environmental literacy training over a period of 6 weeks. Complete post-tests 6 months after the training sessions have concluded.
primary_outcomes: Change in Environmental Literacy Scale Scores
title: The Effect of Theory of Planned Behavior-Based Environmental Literacy Education on Ecological Footprint, Global Climate Change, and Sustainable Environmental Awareness

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Avatar therapy, a virtual reality-based psychotherapy, reduces cannabis use in young adults (18 to 35 years old) with early phase psychosis who use high-potency cannabis on a near-daily basis. The trial will be conducted at 4 Canadian sites (Montreal, Halifax, London, Ottawa).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is Avatar therapy associated with a reduction in cannabis use from baseline to post-treatment?
* Are these reductions maintained during the 1-year follow-up?

Participants will:

* Receive 8 weekly, one-hour, individual sessions of Avatar therapy, in addition to their usual care.
* Complete assessment visits at baseline and approximately 3, 6, 9 and 12 months later (questionnaires on cannabis use, clinical interviews, cognitive testing and urine drug screens)
* For exploratory purposes, participants will undergo brain MRI at baseline and at 12 months
lead_sponsor: Ciusss de L'Est de l'Île de Montréal
title: Avatar Therapy for Cannabis Use in Early Phase Psychosis: A Multisite Trial

brief_summary: This study tested whether adding manual therapy to rehabilitation after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) surgery could reduce knee pain and improve knee function. Fifty-five adults aged 18 to 40 were randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups received the same exercises and cold-pack treatment three times a week for eight weeks. One group also received manual therapy, including patellar mobilization (gently moving the kneecap) and scar tissue massage. Knee pain and function were assessed before treatment and again at eight weeks.
interventions: Experimental Group (exercise therapy, cold pack application, patellar mobilization and scar tissue massage)
Control Group( exercise therapy and cold pack application)
title: Effectiveness of Manual Therapy Application in Patients Who Have Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction

brief_summary:
People having heart surgery can face many physical and emotional challenges before and after the operation. They may need ongoing support to recover well, stay active, and avoid complications. The IReMoS study will evaluate a digital platform that uses ready-to-use technologies to support patients throughout their care journey, from home-based preparation before surgery to coaching after the operation and the final return home.

The IReMoS study is a prospective, single-centre randomized controlled trial that will start enrolling 223 participants. Adults aged 18-75 who are scheduled for planned heart surgery will be eligible if their surgery is at least two weeks after they give consent to take part. Participants in the intervention group will use the IReMoS digital platform that will provide virtual coaching for breathing and physical exercises, personalised educational information, and remote monitoring using a smartwatch and a smart shirt with built-in sensors.

The main goal of the study is to find out whether the use of the platform can reduce complications within three months after surgery. These complications include breathing problems, wound infections, worsening heart failure, and unexpected hospital readmissions. The study will also look at other outcomes, including death within three months, length of hospital stay, quality of life, anxiety, physical ability, and time spent moving. In addition, the researchers will assess how easy the platform is to use and how often technical problems occur.

Moreover, data collected in the study may also help future research develop "digital twins" of patients. These could eventually be used to predict how well a patient's physical and breathing functions will recover after surgery and identify those at higher risk of complications.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS San Gerardo dei Tintori
title: Integrated Rehabilitation & Monitoring Strategies in Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary: This study will assess whether regional anesthesia treatment combined with continuous pressure monitoring can safely control pain in patients having surgery for certain types of broken-leg fractures. A medical device, known as the MY01 Continuous Compartmental Pressure Monitor, will continuously monitor pressure in the leg muscle for up to 48 hours after surgery to help detect acute compartment syndrome (ACS), a serious complication. Hospital personnel will regularly examine the patient's fractured leg, assess pain, and ask the patient how satisfied they are with their pain relief.
primary_outcomes: Patient Perception of Pain Management: APS-POQ-R Questionnaire
Patient Perception of Pain Management: VAS Pain Scores
title: The Use of Nerve Blocks and Ongoing Pressure Monitoring for Tibia Fracture Management

brief_summary:
Primary Objective The main purpose of this study is to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of two multicomponent intervention protocols, both consisting of physiotherapy combined with cognitive training targeting either memory or executive functions, in improving global cognitive functioning in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD).

The goal is to provide scientific evidence on the effectiveness of these intervention strategies in addressing difficulties in overall cognitive functioning, contributing to the development of more targeted and personalized rehabilitation approaches for patients with PD.

Secondary Objectives The secondary objective is to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of the two multicomponent interventions in improving specific cognitive functions (memory, attention, executive functions), motor functioning (balance, gait, upper limb function), and the level of autonomy in patients with PD. The results will also be compared with those obtained in a group receiving physiotherapy alone.
title: Innovative Treatments in the Care of Patients With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: Determination of efficacy and safety of Monopolar Basivertebral Nerve Ablation with application of Autologous Bone Marrow Aspirate Concentrate for Axial Low Back Pain treatment, including the method optimization.
title: Monopolar Basivertebral Nerve Ablation for Axial Low Back Pain With Application of Autologous Bone Marrow Aspirate Concentrate

brief_summary: This study is a prospective cohort study aimed at comparing the effective optical zone (EOZ), higher-order aberrations (HOAs), the predictability of central corneal stromal thickness reduction, and other optical parameters of SMILE under different machine-programmed optical zone settings (small optical zone: less than 6.5mm; medium optical zone: between 6.5mm and 6.8mm; large optical zone: more than 6.8mm). The results from this study are expected to help myopic patients choose the most appropriate machine-programmed optical zone when undergoing SMILE laser refractive surgery. This will allow for better preservation of corneal tissue thickness post-surgery, with improved visual quality and fewer complications at the same time.
primary_outcomes: predictability of central corneal stromal thickness reduction
title: Follow up of Clinical Outcomes in Patients Receiving Small-incision Lenticule Extraction (SMILE)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether checking the breathing tube (endotracheal tube) cuff pressure every 12 hours works as well as checking it every 8 hours in adults on a ventilator in the surgical intensive care unit. Keeping cuff pressure between 20 and 30 cmH₂O helps prevent injury to the windpipe and stops secretions leaking into the lungs, which can cause ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does cuff pressure drop more over 7 days when it is checked every 12 hours rather than every 8 hours?
* Is there a difference in how many patients develop VAP or lung collapse (atelectasis) on ultrasound within 7 days?

Researchers will also look at whether head position, body position and tracheal suctioning are linked to drops in cuff pressure.

Participants will be adults in the surgical ICU at Hospital Pakar Universiti Sains Malaysia who are expected to need a ventilator for at least 48 hours. They will be randomly assigned to cuff-pressure checks every 8 hours or every 12 hours. At each check, the pressure is measured with a manometer and reset to 25 cmH₂O if it is outside 20-30 cmH₂O. Patients will be followed for up to 7 days.
primary_outcomes: Mean Reduction in Endotracheal Tube (ETT) Cuff Pressure Over Time
Number of participants with ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
Number of participants with atelectasis on lung ultrasound
title: Comparison of Mean Pressure Reduction in Endotracheal Tube (ETT) Cuff Pressure Monitoring at 8-Hourly Versus 12-Hourly Intervals in Surgical ICU Patients: Effects on Ventilator Associated Pneumonia (VAP).

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare the efficacy of letrozole versus cervical Foleys in combination with prostaglandin E1 for the termination of pregnancy in the second trimester
title: Comparison of Letrozole Versus Cervical Foley in Combination With Prostaglandin E1 for Termination of Pregnancy in Second Trimester

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of an exercise snacking approach on functional capacity, cardiorespiratory responses, dyspnea severity, and psychosocial parameters in individuals with pulmonary hypertension. The effects of a home-based exercise snacking program consisting of short bouts of aerobic and strengthening exercises distributed throughout the day will be compared with those of a control group receiving patient education.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Is there a difference in functional capacity between individuals with pulmonary hypertension who participate in an exercise snacking program and those who receive patient education?

Is there a difference between these two groups in terms of cardiorespiratory responses, dyspnea severity, and psychosocial parameters?

Participants will:

Be assigned to either an exercise snacking group or a control group receiving patient education for 8 weeks.

Participate in an 8-week home-based exercise snacking program consisting of short bouts of aerobic and strengthening exercises performed intermittently throughout the day, three times per day, five days per week, if assigned to the exercise group.

Undergo assessments of functional capacity, cardiorespiratory responses, dyspnea severity, and psychosocial parameters at baseline and at the end of the 8-week intervention period.
title: Effects of Exercise Snacks on Functional Capacity, Cardiorespiratory Responses, Dyspnea and Psychosocial Parameters in Individuals With Pulmonary Hypertension

brief_summary: To evaluate whether adding bilateral RSB to standardized morphine PCA analgesia reduces morphine consumption in the first 24 hours and improves clinical recovery outcomes compared to morphine PCA alone.
primary_outcomes: Morphine consumption in the first 24 hours
title: Rectus Sheath Block as an Add-On to Morphine PCA for Pain Relief After Emergency Midline Laparotomy: A Randomized Controlled Study

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and activity of 2X-121 with standard-of-care chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant setting for patients with colorectal cancer with liver metastases undergoing curative intent oligometastatic liver resection. The co-primary endpoints are change in tumor cell CD44 expression and change in tumor cell beta-catenin levels in colorectal liver metastases following treatment with 2X-121 and to assess safety and toxicities. Secondary endpoints include 1-year event-free survival and ctDNA negativity for 6 months postoperatively.
lead_sponsor: Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center at Johns Hopkins
primary_outcomes: Number of participants experiencing grade 3 or above drug-related toxicities
title: Neoadjuvant 2X-121 Plus Standard-of-Care Chemotherapy in Patients With Oligometastatic Colorectal Cancer to the Liver Undergoing Curative-Intent Surgery

brief_summary:
Mucinous cell adenocarcinoma of the rectum is a histopathological subtype of rectal cancer first described in 1923 and characterised by the presence of mucin-producing tumour cells in the rectum, with extracellular mucin representing more than 50% of the tumour composition. Mucinous rectal adenocarcinomas have a higher tendency to be diagnosed at an advanced stage, metastasise to regional lymph nodes, recur locally, cause peritoneal carcinomatosis, and have a worse prognosis compared to non-mucinous adenocarcinomas.

This multicenter study aims to assess the differences between mucinous and non-mucinous locally advanced rectal cancer responses to the neoadjuvant treatment and surgery in a curative setting. Downstaging differences will be evaluated by comparing the pre-neoadjuvant and post-neoadjuvant magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In contrast, post-surgical differences will be assessed by comparing the pathological complete response, the tumour regression grade, the radicality of the surgery, the local and distant recurrence risk and the overall and cancer-specific survival.

.
title: Differences of Mucinous Versus Non-mucinous Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Response

brief_summary:
Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is the most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb, resulting from compression of the median nerve under the transverse carpal ligament at the wrist. It commonly presents with pain, numbness, tingling, reduced grip strength, and impaired hand function, which significantly affect daily activities and quality of life. Conservative management is considered the first-line treatment for mild to moderate CTS, with median nerve mobilization being widely used to improve neural mobility and reduce pain. However, evidence suggests that median nerve mobilization is effective for relief of symptoms, while its impact on grip strength and long-term functional improvement remains inconsistent. CTS also involves muscular weakness of the wrist and forearm muscles; combining neural techniques with strengthening exercises may provide superior outcomes. The objective of the current study is to determine the effects of median nerve mobilizations combined with eccentric forearm exercises on pain, grip strength, and hand function in patients with mild to moderate carpal tunnel syndrome.

A single-blinded randomized control trial will be conducted .46 participants aged 18-65 years, diagnosed with mild to moderate CTS confirmed by nerve conduction studies, will be recruited using a non-probability convenience sampling technique in the study. Participants will be randomly allocated into two groups using the concealed envelope method. Group A is the experimental group that will receive median nerve mobilization, eccentric forearm exercises, along conventional physiotherapy, while Group B is the control group, which will receive median nerve mobilization with conventional physiotherapy only. Both groups will receive treatment twice weekly for 10 weeks. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, at 5 weeks, and at 10 weeks. Pain will be measured by Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), hand grip strength measured using a JAMAR hand dynamometer, and hand functions assess by the Functional Status Scale of the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ). Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 27.
interventions: Median nerve mobilizations along conventional therapy was assigned to the active comparator group
Median nerve mobilizations along conventional therapy in addition to eccentric forearm exercises which include following exercises was assigned to experimental group
title: Median Nerve Mobilizations Combined With Eccentric Forearm Exercises in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

brief_summary:
The Brownsville Wellness Program for Blood Pressure (B-WELL BP) is a community-based Food Is Medicine pilot study designed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a culturally tailored nutrition education program for adults with elevated blood pressure or hypertension in Brownsville, Brooklyn, New York.

The 6-week program will be delivered in partnership with the Brownsville Community Culinary Center (BCCC) and will incorporate nutrition education based on the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) eating pattern, cooking demonstrations, behavioral goal setting, weekly produce prescriptions, and a potassium-enriched salt substitute to support sodium reduction. The program will emphasize affordable, culturally relevant foods and practical strategies for improving dietary habits.

The study will enroll \~108 participants across three sequential cohorts, with a goal of approximately 90 participants completing the program. All participants will receive the intervention. There will be no randomized assignment or control group.

The primary dietary outcome will be change in diet quality, assessed using the rapid Prime Diet Quality Score (rPDQS). Secondary and exploratory outcomes will include changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, fruit and vegetable intake, body weight, and other health-related measures. The study will also evaluate recruitment, retention, attendance, participant engagement, intervention acceptability, implementation fidelity, and program costs.
title: Brownsville Wellness Program for Blood Pressure

brief_summary: This study evaluated whether different sitting positions during spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery affect the success of spinal puncture. In this prospective, randomized controlled trial, 600 pregnant women were assigned to four groups, with 150 participants in each group. The study compared spinal puncture outcomes across four sitting positions, including the pendant position. The main outcome was needle-bone contact during spinal puncture. Additional assessments included the ease of identifying anatomical landmarks, procedural characteristics, and patient satisfaction. The study aimed to determine whether patient positioning could improve the technical performance of spinal anesthesia during cesarean delivery.
interventions: Legs Parallel to the Operating Table Position
primary_outcomes: Spinal Puncture Success Assessed by Needle-Bone Contact
title: Effect of Sitting Positions on Spinal Puncture Success During Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to understand the effects of modified Brostrom repair with suture tape augmentation (surgical treatment variable) and photobiomodulation therapy (rehabilitation variable) on the clinical outcomes of lateral ankle ligament repair to improve functional recovery and enhance return to duty / activity rates of active-duty service members and civilians alike, as applicable.

The main question it aims to answer is whether or not combining a modified Brostrom repair with suture tape augmentation with photobiomodulation therapy will enhance the clinical outcomes for lateral ankle ligament repair due to enhanced mechanical stability from suture tape augmentation, and reduced pain and inflammation, enhanced blood flow, and enhanced collagen production from photobiomodulation therapy.

Up to 300 male and female participants who are at least 18 years of age at screening who have been diagnosed with chronic ankle instability and meet all other eligibility requirements will be enrolled.
title: Surgical Technique and Photobiomodulation Therapy for Chronic Ankle Instability

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the effectiveness of Traditional Articulation Therapy (TAT) and Perceptual Articulation Therapy (PAT) in improving speech sound production among children with Cerebral Palsy (CP). TAT focuses mainly on repeated practice and production of target speech sounds, whereas PAT emphasizes listening, sound discrimination, and identification of correct and incorrect speech sounds. The study will determine which approach produces greater improvement in speech sound accuracy and speech intelligibility, providing evidence to support effective speech therapy practices for children with CP.
primary_outcomes: Effects of Traditional Versus Perception Articulation Therapy for speech sound Disorder in children with Cerebral Palsy
title: Traditional Versus Perception Articulation Therapy for Speech Sounds Disorders in Children With Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
Coronary stent implantation is a common treatment for coronary artery disease. However, current methods used to evaluate implanted stents and detect complications such as in-stent restenosis are generally invasive and may require ionizing radiation.

The WAEVE® device is an investigational, non-invasive, non-ionizing medical device that uses microwave interferometry to assess implanted coronary stents. The NIMBLE-II study is designed to evaluate the performance of a new pre-measurement feature incorporated into WAEVE® that detects heartbeat-synchronous microwave reflections and helps distinguish true stent-related signals from non-cardiac or artifactual signals. By confirming the cardiac origin of the detected reflection, this feature is intended to improve the robustness and reliability of WAEVE® measurements and reduce the risk of false detections arising from non-cardiac or artifactual reflections.

This prospective, multicenter, single-arm clinical investigation will enroll adults undergoing elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Participants will undergo WAEVE® measurements before PCI and, when a single coronary stent is implanted, after PCI. The study aims to generate technical and clinical evidence supporting the reliability and robustness of the WAEVE® pre-measurement feature under real clinical conditions.
primary_outcomes: Heartbeat-Synchronous Signal Detection Rate in Post-PCI Acquisitions
title: Evaluation of WAEVE® Pre-Measurement Feature for Detection of Implanted Coronary Stents in Patients Undergoing Elective PCI

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of an individualized occupational therapy program guided by the Canadian Model of Occupational Performance (CMOP) in adults with upper-extremity burns. Participants received conventional burn rehabilitation. The intervention group additionally received an individualized occupational therapy program three times per week for eight weeks, while the control group received individualized guidance and weekly consultations alongside conventional rehabilitation. The study assessed occupational performance, hand function, and health-related quality of life using standardized assessment tools. The findings are intended to provide information about the contribution of individualized occupational therapy to the rehabilitation of adults with upper-extremity burns.
title: Canadian Model of Occupational Performance-Guided Occupational Therapy in Adults With Upper-Extremity Burns

brief_summary: This study employed a randomized controlled clinical design to examine the efficacy of a digital Nature Psychotherapy intervention in individuals with obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and to compare the roles of human counselors versus GenAI in providing feedback on psychological diaries. A total of 200 participants (N = 200) are planned to be recruited and randomly assigned to four groups of equal size (n = 50). The first group received a four-week digital self-help intervention supplemented by psychological diary feedback from human counselors; the second group received the same four-week digital self-help intervention, with psychological diary feedback provided by a GenAI; the third group completed only the four-week digital self-help intervention, without any psychological diary feedback; and the fourth group served as the control group, receiving a four-week general psychological knowledge course without psychological diary feedback.
interventions: Digital intervention based on Nature Psychotherapy
Psychological diary feedback provided by human counselors
Psychological diary feedback provided by GenAI
title: GenAI Feedback in Digital OCD Intervention

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how symptoms and medication use change in people living with dementia who receive the Technology-Enabled Integrated Care Pathway (Tech-ICP). Participants are adults aged 50 or older living in Ontario long-term care homes. Tech-ICP helps care teams assess dementia-related symptoms and choose care strategies suited to each person. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do agitation and other dementia-related symptoms become less severe after 3, 6, and 12 months?
* Are fewer participants taking several psychiatric medications at the same time to treat these symptoms?

Participants will already be receiving Tech-ICP through a separate care improvement initiative. Joining the research study will not change their treatment.

Researchers will follow participants for up to 12 months. They will review health records and collect information through assessments at the start and after 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 months. Residents, home staff, and participating care partners will provide information about residents' symptoms and well-being. Care partners will also answer questions about their experience of providing care.

Participants may choose to take part in additional research activities:

* Give blood samples at the start and after 12 months.
* Wear a wrist sensor that records sleep, movement, heart rate, and other body signals.
* Wear a headband that records brain electrical activity and blood oxygen changes at the start and after 12 months.

These optional activities will help researchers understand how changes in the body and brain relate to dementia-related symptoms.
lead_sponsor: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health
primary_outcomes: Change in Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S) score
Clinical Global Impression of Change (CGIC) score
Change in Cohen-Mansfield Agitation Inventory (CMAI) score
Change in Neuropsychiatric Inventory Questionnaire (NPI-Q) score
title: The Technology-Enabled Integrated Care Pathway (Tech-ICP) for Dementia in Long-Term Care

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the impact of preoperative cyberchondria-compulsive and anxiety-inducing online health information seeking-on acute and longitudinal clinical outcomes in patients undergoing fluoroscopy-guided lumbar transforaminal epidural steroid injection (TFESI) for unilateral lumbar radicular pain.

Patients with lumbar disc herniation frequently search for intervention details and prognosis online. This behavior may trigger health anxiety, procedural fear, and nocebo-related responses that potentially compromise therapeutic efficacy. Eligible adult patients undergoing elective lumbar TFESI will be evaluated preoperatively for cyberchondria severity (CSS-12), surgical fear (SFQ), anxiety (BAI), pain catastrophizing (PCS), baseline radicular pain (NRS), and functional disability (ODI). Following the procedure, acute pain relief and immediate recovery will be assessed at 30 minutes in the post-anesthesia care unit. Follow-up evaluations will be conducted at 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months post-procedure to determine changes in pain intensity (NRS), neuropathic pain components (DN4), and functional disability (ODI). The primary objective is to investigate whether higher baseline cyberchondria independently predicts diminished pain reduction and poorer 3-month functional recovery.
primary_outcomes: Correlation between baseline cyberchondria severity and post-procedure pain intensity changes across follow-ups
title: Impact of Cyberchondria on Outcomes of Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injections

brief_summary:
Cardiogenic shock is a life-threatening condition in which the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs. Changes in how the heart uses energy may contribute to impaired heart function. Ketones provide an alternative energy source for the heart. The investigators hypothesize that increasing ketone availability may improve heart function and reduce the need for medications that support blood pressure and circulation.

KETONES-CS is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial evaluating the feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects of ketone monoester administration in adults with cardiogenic shock.

Sixty participants will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to receive ketone monoester or a comparison solution without ketone monoester (placebo). Study treatment will be given by mouth or through a feeding tube every six hours for up to 72 hours. Ketone monoester doses will be adjusted according to blood ketone levels and safety assessments.

The study will assess whether treatment can be administered as planned, whether target blood ketone levels can be achieved, and whether treatment is safe and well tolerated. It will also explore effects on heart function, the need for medications that support circulation, and blood markers of metabolism and inflammation. Findings will inform the design of future clinical trials.
primary_outcomes: Vasoactive-Inotropic Score Area Under the Curve From 0 to 72 Hours
Cardiac Power Output Area Under the Curve From 0 to 72 Hours
Cardiac Index Area Under the Curve From 0 to 72 Hours
title: Ketone Monoester Administration in Cardiogenic Shock

brief_summary:
This pilot study aims to evaluate the effects, tolerability, and feasibility of a six-week therapeutic exercise program incorporating blood flow restriction (BFR) at 50% limb occlusion pressure in individuals with Parkinson's disease.

The study will use a single-group, non-randomized, pre-post interventional design, with both individual case-level and group-level analyses. Participants will complete 12 supervised exercise sessions over six weeks (two sessions per week) at the Faculty of Physiotherapy in Pontevedra, University of Vigo, Spain.

The intervention will consist of progressive lower-limb resistance exercises performed with BFR using pneumatic cuffs positioned proximally on the lower limbs. The cuffs will be inflated to 50% limb occlusion pressure during exercise sets and deflated during rest periods. Exercise intensity and complexity will be individually adjusted after the first three weeks according to participants' tolerance and perceived exertion.

Assessments will be conducted at baseline (week 0) and after the intervention (week 7). Outcome measures will include maximal isometric knee extension and flexion strength, functional mobility assessed using the Timed Up and Go test, performance on the Five Times Sit-to-Stand test, postural stability assessed through center-of-pressure parameters, and dynamic plantar pressure distribution during walking.

Tolerability and feasibility will be explored through perceived exertion, participant satisfaction, and the ability to complete the exercise protocol. Individual responses will be described alongside group-level changes using appropriate descriptive and exploratory statistical analyses.

The findings will provide preliminary information on the clinical responses and practical feasibility of BFR-assisted therapeutic exercise in individuals with Parkinson's disease and may inform the design of future controlled clinical trials.
primary_outcomes: Change in Maximal Isometric Knee Extension Strength
Adherence to the Blood Flow Restriction Exercise Program
Independent Use of Blood Flow Restriction Cuffs
title: Blood Flow Restriction Therapy in Patients With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary:
Millions of individuals worldwide suffer from migraines, a common and incapacitating neurological condition. Frequent, moderate to severe headaches are its defining feature, and symptoms including nausea, vomiting, and photophobia are frequently present as well. Researchers are looking into better ways to prevent and cure migraines because of the condition's widespread prevalence1. A major component of long-term care of migraines is preventing recurrent bouts, even though acute therapies are frequently employed to cure individual attacks. Drugs include β-blockers, antiepileptics, antidepressants, and more recent biologic medicines are effective preventive measures2. Amitriptyline is one among these that has been used extensively because of its shown effectiveness and safety record. Tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) amitriptyline is authorised for the preventative treatment of migraines. Neurotransmitters including serotonin and norepinephrine, which are thought to be involved in the pathophysiology of migraines, are modulated as part of its mechanism of action3. Amitriptyline's adverse effects, which include drowsiness, weight gain, and anticholinergic effects, frequently restrict its use despite its effectiveness. Coenzyme Q10 is a naturally occurring antioxidant that has a role in cell energy production and mitochondrial activity4. According to recent studies, the pathophysiology of migraines may be related to a CoQ10 shortage. Supplementing with CoQ10 has been shown in several studies to lessen the frequency and intensity of migraine attacks. Because of its impact on inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, CoQ10 may help prevent migraines. Combining Amitriptyline and CoQ10 may increase their efficacy in preventing migraines because of their different modes of action5-6. Amitriptyline treats abnormalities in neurotransmitters, and CoQ10 tackles malfunction in the mitochondria. For migraine sufferers who might not react well to amitriptyline alone, this combination may offer a more comprehensive therapeutic strategy and enhance results7. Amitriptyline's effectiveness in lowering the frequency of migraine attacks has been validated by numerous clinical trials. Amitriptyline was shown to be considerably more effective than a placebo in lowering the number of migraine days per month in a randomised controlled trial8. However, common side effects like weight gain, dry mouth, and tiredness can make it harder for patients to comply9. The function of CoQ10 in preventing migraines has been the subject of numerous investigations.

The main purpose of this study is to assess the efficacy of Amitriptyline plus coenzyme q10 with Amitriptyline alone in migraine prevention and decreasing pain episodes.
title: Amitriptyline Plus Coenzyme Q10 Versus Amitriptyline Alone for Migraine Prevention

brief_summary:
The interaction between dysregulated dopamine, serotonin, and glutamate neurocircuits exacerbates the neuropathology of schizophrenia. Previous studies found that some glutamate NMDA receptor (NMDAR)-enhancing agents were able to improve clinical symptoms of patients with chronic schizophrenia.

Whether combined treatment of an NMDA-enhancing agent and a serotonin/dopamine modulator (SDM) can be better than an NMDA-enhancing agent alone deserves study.
primary_outcomes: Change of Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS)
title: Integrated Modulation of Dopamine, Serotonin, and Glutamate Neurocircuits for the Treatment of Schizophrenia

brief_summary:
Injuries to the small nerves in the fingers are common and can affect feeling, cause pain, and limit hand function. These nerves are usually repaired during surgery by carefully stitching the nerve ends together. While this approach often restores basic protective feeling, many people do not regain normal sensation in the injured finger, and recovery can be unpredictable.

This study looks at the postoperative outcomes of a newer surgical coaptation device called Nerve Tape, which allows surgeons to reconnect injured finger nerves without using stitches. Instead, the device gently holds the nerve ends together using a flexible wrap designed to support healing while minimizing additional trauma to the nerve. Early laboratory and clinical studies suggest that this approach may shorten surgery time and provide stable nerve repair, but more information is needed about how patients recover after this type of repair.

The purpose of this study is to better understand how patients do after finger nerve repair using this suture-free device. Specifically, the study examines how well feeling returns, how much pain patients experience, and how hand function improves over time. Sensation, pain levels, and hand function are measured during routine follow-up visits over the first six months after surgery. The information gained from this study will help improve knowledge about outcomes after finger nerve repair and support future research comparing different repair methods.
title: Postoperative Outcomes of Digital Nerve Coaptations Using a Sutureless Coaptation Device

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate a psychological intervention based on the ACCEPT model for adults who have experienced termination of pregnancy due to fetal anomaly in Portugal. It aims to determine whether the intervention improves grief-related and psychological outcomes compared with treatment as usual, and to explore whether baseline individual, relational, and psychosocial characteristics influence treatment response.

The study will use a two-arm randomized controlled design, with a planned sample of 116 participants. Eligible participants will be aged 18 years or older, able to communicate in Portuguese, and have experienced the termination either as the person who underwent the procedure or as their partner. Recruitment will take place through collaborating patient associations and support networks.

After informed consent and baseline assessment, participants will be randomly allocated to one of two conditions. The ACCEPT condition will comprise 12 weekly individual online psychological sessions, lasting approximately one hour each, over three months. Sessions will address grief reactions, emotional regulation, difficult thoughts and memories, continuing bonds, interpersonal relationships, and adjustment to life following the loss. Participants in the treatment-as-usual condition will have access to support ordinarily provided by partner organizations, including professionally facilitated sharing groups.

Assessments will take place at baseline, immediately after the three-month intervention period, and three months later. Standardized questionnaires will measure perinatal grief, prolonged grief symptoms, psychological distress, psychological flexibility, continuing bonds, and relationship satisfaction where applicable. Baseline assessments will additionally collect sociodemographic information and contextual characteristics of the loss.

Longitudinal mixed models will estimate differences between conditions while accounting for baseline scores and repeated assessments. Exploratory analyses will examine potential moderators of treatment effects and psychological flexibility as a possible mechanism of change. The findings will inform the development of more individualized psychological support following termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly.

Participation will be voluntary and confidential, and participants may discontinue without penalty. Both conditions will include procedures for identifying significant distress and referring participants for additional care when needed.
lead_sponsor: ISPA - Instituto Universitario de Ciencias Psicologicas, Sociais e da Vida
primary_outcomes: Perinatal grief severity assessed using the 33-item Perinatal Grief Scale Short Version (PGS)
title: Tailoring Psychological Intervention Following Termination of Pregnancy for Foetal Anomaly

brief_summary: The Four Evaluation Statement (FOREST) study is an ongoing observational registry at Fundación Jiménez Díaz University Hospital for adults with rectal adenocarcinoma who are assessed by a multidisciplinary team and have an indication for neoadjuvant treatment or a selected organ-preservation strategy. The registry records routine care, including treatment, response, rectal organ preservation, recurrence, survival, and quality of life. Treatment decisions are made by patients and their clinical teams. The registry does not assign treatments. The current reporting period will include participants enrolled through January 1, 2028, and follow-up available through that date. The clinical registry continues beyond that reporting period.
lead_sponsor: Instituto de Investigación Sanitaria de la Fundación Jiménez Díaz
title: Organ Preservation in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate, in patients who present to our emergency department, are diagnosed with paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT), and in whom adenosine is to be used as the first dose to restore sinus rhythm by the decision of the physician, whether there is a difference in the success of conversion to sinus rhythm between administering adenosine as a standard 6 mg dose regardless of body weight and administering adenosine calculated according to the patient's body weight. The only difference between the arms is the amount of adenosine administered: routinely 6 mg regardless of body weight in the standard treatment arm, and 0.1 mg/kg determined on a weight basis in the other arm. The primary endpoint is achievement of sinus rhythm persisting for at least 10 minutes; the secondary endpoint is adenosine-related adverse effects.
lead_sponsor: Ankara Ataturk Sanatorium Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Rate of Conversion to Sinus Rhythm After First-Dose Adenosine
title: Comparison of Sinus Rhythm Conversion Success Rates of Standard and Weight-Based First-Dose Adenosine in Patients With Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia

brief_summary:
This post-market, prospective, open-label, observational (non-interventional) study is designed to evaluate the performance and safety of AnGelHA ESTIMA in routine clinical practice.

Subjects over 18 years old, willing to undergo non-surgical aesthetic procedure with AnGelHA ESTIMA for the correction of superficial fine wrinkles, will be offered to participate in the study. The investigators will enroll any subject who receives at least one treatment with AnGelHA ESTIMA and who has provided informed consent. They will follow their routine practice regarding injection technique, volume, and subject follow-up. Treatments will be performed for a single injection area or for multiple areas where correction is requested, subject to the advice of the practitioner and in accordance with the product intended use and conditions. Any of the treatment areas listed in Section 9 can be treated during the study, depending on the subject's needs and subject to the practitioner's discretion, as per routine practice. The area to be treated and the injection characteristics - volume, depth, technique and distance between injection points - are all left to the discretion of the practitioner and will be recorded in the case report form (CRF).

The study protocol includes three initial visits performed 2-4 weeks apart (Visit 1 - Day 0; Visit 2 - Week 2-4; Visit 3 - Week 4-8) and two follow-up visits at Months 5-6 and Months 10-12 after Day 0 (Visit 4 and Visit 5, respectively). Treatment sessions at Visits 2 and 3 are performed according to the subject's needs and are optional, as per the observational study design; performance and safety assessments are performed at all scheduled visits. Additional visits are allowed at any time throughout the follow-up period at the subject's request or when deemed necessary. At each visit, performance and safety will be evaluated.
primary_outcomes: The proportion of subjects deemed improved
title: Post Market Study of Safety and Performance of AnGelHA ESTIMA for the Correction of Superficial Fine Wrinkles

brief_summary: The aim of the project is to improve our knowledge on the stability and temporal dynamics of the Flemish female microbiome (vagina, skin and saliva) in relation to different lifestyle factors and environmental conditions and to establish certain individual and social risk factors that can influence the healthy microbiome. Therefore, microbial DNA from swabs will be isolated via commercially available DNA extraction kits, followed by Illumina MiSeq sequencing or metagenomic shotgun sequencing in order to identify the microbial species present in these samples and their functionalities. Additionally, microorganisms will be cultured and their metabolic capacities will be investigated. Special attention will go to microbial species that are overrepresented in the healthy populations as potential health promoting microbes (i.e. probiotics).
primary_outcomes: Differences in microbial communities colonizing the vagina, skin and saliva between healthy individuals
title: Integrated Genetic and Functional Analysis of the Female Microbiome in a Flemish Cohort - Part 2

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare two commonly used chemotherapy options, oral tegafur-uracil (UFUR) and intravenous 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), when combined with immune checkpoint inhibitor-based treatment in patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC).

A total of 30 patients will participate in this study. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either oral UFUR or intravenous 5-FU, with 15 patients in each group. Both medications are existing clinical treatment options. Other aspects of cancer treatment and routine follow-up will be determined by the treating physician according to each patient's clinical condition.

In addition to routine clinical care, participants will provide extra blood samples before treatment, at week 6, and at week 12. These samples will be used to measure circulating tumor cells (CTCs), which are cancer cells that may be found in the bloodstream, and to examine a marker called PD-L1 on these cells.

The study will explore whether changes in circulating tumor cells and PD-L1 are associated with treatment response, disease progression, and survival. It will also collect preliminary information on the clinical outcomes and safety of the two treatment options.

The findings may help researchers better understand the potential of blood-based monitoring for evaluating early treatment response in patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer.
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
primary_outcomes: Change in Circulating Tumor Cell (CTC) Count Over 12 Weeks
title: Oral Tegafur-Uracil Versus Intravenous 5-Fluorouracil in Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Cancer

brief_summary:

brief_summary: Sacroiliac joint plays a crucial role in load transmission between the spine and pelvis, and dysfunction may occur due to malalignment, hypomobility, or hypermobility. Abnormal functional activities such as bending, lifting, and sustained lordotic postures can alter pelvic biomechanics, leading to pain and stiffness in the sacroiliac region. Common SIJD is anterior innominate rotation which is the major risk factor for idiopathic LBP. In AID, innominate bones move anteriorly on the sacrum that is in the counter-nutation. Unilateral AID occurs when musculature of hip flexors, trunk extensors, hip extensors and abdominal muscles are unbalanced1 Muscle Energy Technique (MET) is widely used to correct innominate rotations through controlled isometric contractions, producing both biomechanical and neurophysiological effects. Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) is another effective approach that utilizes diagonal movement patterns to stimulate proprioceptors, improve trunk stability, muscle strength, and coordination. The aim of this study is to evaluate the comparative effects of METs versus proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation on pain, functional disability and range of motion in patients with sacroiliac joint dysfunction.
title: Effects of Muscle Energy Techniques Versus Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation on Pain, Range of Motion and Functional Disability in Patients With Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction.

brief_summary:
* This is a multicenter, prospective, open-label,randomised controlled trial to compare Spot-marking and Clip-marking TAD (targeted axillary dissection) in patients with initially node-positive breast cancer after neoadjuvant systemic treatments. Additionally, this trial still aims to explore the feasibility of utilizing PA/US（photoacoustic/ultrasound） device to identify Spot-ink marked lymph nodes.
* Key Details ：

  （1）Participants: 486 women (aged 18-80)with pathologically diagnosed primary invasive breast cancer (cT1N1M0 - cT3N3aM0) and axillary lymph node metastasis.

  (2) Design:

Patients are randomized 1:1 to two groups:

* Group Spot-TAD (Spot-ink Marking TAD) :Patients receive ultasound-guided Spot-marking of axillary lymph node metastasis befor the neoadjuvant systemic treatments.Then, patients receive the standard neoadjuvant systemic treatments.After the neoadjuvant systemic treatments, patients receive TAD following with ALND(axillary lymph node dissection).
* Group Clip-TAD (Clip Marking TAD) :Patients receive ultasound-guided Clip-marking of axillary lymph node metastasis befor theneoadjuvant systemic treatments .Then, patients receive the standard neoadjuvant systemic treatments .After the neoadjuvant systemic treatments , patients receive TAD following with ALND.
* Photoacoustic imaging: Utilizing PA/US (photoacoustic/ ultrasound )device （The Resona Y ultrasound diagnostic system ，Shenzhen Mindray Bio-Medical Electronics Co., Ltd.，China）to perform photoacoustic imaging on 20 - 30 patients in Group Spot-TAD.

brief_summary:
The SSW-DCB study will test whether a slow balloon inflation technique reduces the need for a stent during a coronary procedure in adults with coronary artery disease who are scheduled for drug-coated balloon treatment.

Before using a drug-coated balloon, doctors use a separate balloon to prepare the narrowed area of the artery. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with an equal chance of joining either group. In one group, doctors will use the Slow Up, Slow Down, and Wait (SSW) technique, which involves gradually increasing the balloon pressure, holding it briefly, and then gradually releasing the pressure. In the other group, doctors will use the usual balloon inflation technique.

After preparing the artery, doctors will check whether it is suitable for treatment with a drug-coated balloon. If the artery meets the study criteria for needing a stent, a stent may be placed during the procedure. This is called bailout stenting. The main question is whether fewer participants in the SSW group need bailout stenting.

Follow-up visits or calls are planned at 1, 6, 9, and 12 months after the procedure. A repeat coronary angiogram is planned at 12 months to check the treated area. Longer-term follow-up will collect information about heart-related and bleeding events.
interventions: Slow Up, Slow Down, and Wait Balloon Inflation
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Undergoing Intraprocedural Bailout Stenting
title: Slow Up, Slow Down, and Wait Balloon Inflation Before Planned Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease

This prospective observational study aims to compare the effects of erector spinae plane (ESP) block, epidural analgesia, and standard systemic analgesia on postoperative pain, opioid consumption, patient satisfaction, and recovery in patients undergoing elective lumbar stabilization surgery.

A total of 90 adult patients aged 18-70 years, classified as American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I-III, will be included. Patients will be observed in three groups according to the analgesic method selected as part of routine clinical care: ESP block, epidural analgesia, or standard systemic analgesia.

Postoperative pain will be assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at 30 minutes and 6, 12, and 24 hours after surgery. The primary outcome will be the VAS pain score at 24 hours. Secondary outcomes will include postoperative opioid consumption, rescue analgesia requirements, patient satisfaction, time to first mobilization, postoperative nausea and vomiting, and complications.

The study aims to provide comparative evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of these commonly used analgesic techniques following lumbar stabilization surgery.
