Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Abnormalities in Clinical Laboratory Tests
Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Abnormalities on Abdominal Ultrasound
title: Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Single-Dose KR25102 Tablets in Healthy Adult Participants

brief_summary:
Infants with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at increased risk for delayed neurodevelopment. Multiple etiological explanations have been proposed, as there seems to be a multifactorial interplay of both prenatal and perioperative factors. The main goal of this research project is to focus on peri-operative physiological risk factors in infants with CHD which impair functional brain maturation or elicit brain injury, and subsequently creating a risk model and guidelines for standardized developmental follow-up in this population.

PART 1: investigation of cerebral autoregulation and neurovascular coupling The homeostasis in cerebral blood supply regardless of perfusion pressure, is called Cerebral autoregulation (CAR). Neurovascular coupling (NVC) is the phenomenon in which blood supply increases as a result of increased brain activity in a specific area. At different times in the perioperative phase, these regulatory mechanisms will be estimated based on Electroencephalography (EEG) and Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS), in addition to hemodynamic parameters.

PART 2: cell-free DNA (cfDNA) extraction. Non-invasive monitoring of neuronal degeneration can be performed using cfDNA extraction techniques. Serial measurements of neuronal cfDNA will be used to determine whether and when this neuronal damage has occurred.

PART 3: Prognosis and outcome. These risk factors, supplemented with demographic factors and medications administered, will be combined in an Artificial Intelligence-driven model, thus establishing a risk model for neurodevelopmental outcome. This model will be compared to the current standard-of-care, both structural imaging (ultrasound and MRI) and a clinical developmental assessment at 9 and 24 months of age (Bayley Scales of Infant Development-III).
title: The Predictive Value of Neurovascular Coupling in Infants With Congenital Heart Disease

brief_summary:
Stroke often leads to reduced hand function due to poor motor control, decreased coordination, and limited joint movement, which can make everyday activities difficult to perform. In individuals with hand hemiparesis, rehabilitation plays a key role in improving functional recovery of the affected hand. Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) is commonly used to enhance muscle activation and coordination, while app-based interventions such as the Dexteria application provide engaging, repetitive hand exercises that support motor relearning. In addition, smartphone-based angle measurement offers a simple and objective way to assess joint movement in clinical practice. The purpose of this study is to determine the effects of combining hand PNF with Dexteria app exercises on post-stroke hand function using smartphone-based angle measurement in individuals with hand hemiparesis.

This study will be conducted as a randomized clinical trial at ACME Hospital, Gulberg, Lahore. A non-probability convenient sampling technique will be used to recruit subacute post-stroke. All participants will have pre-diagnosis of stroke by a neurologist. Eligible participants will be randomly allocated into two groups to minimize allocation bias. The experimental group will receive Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) techniques combined with Dexteria app therapy, while the control group will receive conventional hand therapy. Outcome measures will include assessment of wrist, metacarpophalangeal, and interphalangeal joint angles using the Angulus smartphone application, functional hand performance using the Jebsen Taylor Hand Function Test, voluntary hand control assessed through the Brunnstrom hand recovery voluntary control grades, Fugal Meyer Assessment test will be use to assess hand function of patients. PNF and Dexteria app-based treatment plan of 12 weeks will be given to experimental group and 12 weeks treatment plan of conventional therapy will be given to control group. The proposed study aims to investigate the combined effects of therapist-guided Hand PNF and Dexteria app home exercises on hand function after stroke, using smartphone-based angle measurement as the primary assessment tool. Data will be analyzed through SPSS version.
interventions: Hand PNF Combined with Dexteria App Exercises
title: Hand PNF Combined With Dexteria App Exercises on Post-Stroke Hand Function Assessed by Smartphone-Based Angle Measurement

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding Mulligan mobilization with movement (MWM), a manual therapy technique, to a progressive conventional exercise program improves outcomes in adults aged 40 to 65 with early-stage (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1-2) knee osteoarthritis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Mulligan MWM plus exercise reduce knee pain more than exercise alone?
* Does it also improve Q angle, knee proprioception (joint position sense), balance, functional performance, WOMAC scores and quality of life (SF-36)?

Researchers will compare Mulligan MWM plus progressive conventional exercise with progressive conventional exercise alone.

Participants will:

* Attend 2 supervised sessions per week for 6 weeks (12 sessions in total)
* Perform a home exercise program on the days without supervised sessions
* Be assessed at baseline, at month 1 and at month 6
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity during activity (Visual Analogue Scale)
title: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement in Early-Stage Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary:
The Tacrolimus Optimization through FormUlation (TOFU) study will investigate various pharmacological parameters of tacrolimus in kidney transplant recipients.

In simple words, we will investigate the blood concentrations of tacrolimus over a day, using 3 blood samples. In particular, we will compare whole blood tacrolimus concentrations AND intra-cellular tacrolimus concentrations (in leukocytes, also known as white blood cells).
title: Tacrolimus Optimization Through FormUlation

brief_summary:
The BETA project is based on the E3N-Generations cohort, a unique multigenerational cohort in France and one of the few in Europe. The study aims to: (1) characterize serum concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in two generations of French women approximately 25 years apart; (2) identify demographic, anthropometric, reproductive, and lifestyle determinants of PFAS exposure; (3) evaluate correlations between PFAS serum concentrations and endocrine and metabolic biomarkers indicative of early biological effects; and (4) investigate potential intergenerational associations by assessing correlations between mothers' and daughters' PFAS serum concentrations and the relationship between maternal PFAS concentrations and biomarkers measured in adult daughters.

The availability of archived blood samples collected from first-generation participants between 1994 and 1999 and newly collected blood samples from second-generation participants in 2024, together with detailed information on lifestyle, reproductive history, anthropometric characteristics, and health status, provides a unique opportunity to evaluate long-term changes in PFAS exposure and their potential biological effects.
lead_sponsor: Institut National de la Santé Et de la Recherche Médicale, France
primary_outcomes: Correlation between circulating PFAS in mother and her daughter
Correlation Between Serum PFAS Concentrations and Endocrine Biomarkers
Correlation Between Serum PFAS Concentrations and Metabolic Biomarkers
Correlation between Maternal and Daughter PFAS Serum Concentrations
title: Biomarkers Associated to Endocrine Disruptors Exposure: a Transgenerational Approach

brief_summary:
This study is being conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once weekly doses of anvoglutide in participants with overweight and obesity.

In addition to dietary caloric restriction and increased physical activity, study participants will receive either anvoglutide tablets or placebo tablets (placebo looks like anvoglutide tablets but has no active pharmaceutical ingredients). For a fair comparison, study participants are assigned to anvoglutide or placebo randomly by a computer.

The treatment will last for 24 weeks. Anvoglutide will be administered in an up-titration fashion, i.e. the dose of anvoglutide will be gradually increased to reach three target doses so that the participants can tolerate its effect. Participants will have 12 clinic visits including one screening visit and one follow-up visit.

Female participants who are pregnant, breast-feeding or who plan to become pregnant during the study are not allowed to participate in the study. Pregnancy will be checked by blood or urine tests during the study.
primary_outcomes: Change in body weight relative to baseline
title: Efficacy and Safety of Weekly Anvoglutide (ZT006) in Overweight and Obese Participants

brief_summary:
The studies aims summarized are; Aims 1-3) The purpose of this study is to test new MRI computer software and settings that reduce the visual artifact caused by cardiac devices, allowing doctors to better see the structure of the heart, how well the heart and its vessels are functioning, and any scarring of the heart tissue caused by complications such as a heart attack.

Aim 4) closed to enrollment Aim 5) The purpose of this study is to use recently developed MRI techniques to compare heart health of individuals with COVID-19 to people who were asymptomatic. The new MRI techniques used in this experiment may also allow researchers and health care providers to take clearer pictures of the heart in other individuals.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the accuracy and precision of real-time wideband stress CMR in suspected CAD patients with a simulated CIED implantation
To determine the prognostic value of real-time wideband stress CMR in CIED patients
To validate real-time wideband LGE CMR against electroanatomic mapping (EAM) in ICD patients
title: cMR for Patients With CIED

brief_summary: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune disease that causes joint pain, swelling, stiffness, and functional limitations. Hand involvement can substantially affect daily activities. Photobiomodulation therapy combined with static magnetic field (PBMT-sMF) uses light to help modulate inflammation and relieve pain, but the most appropriate treatment dose for rheumatoid arthritis of the hands remains uncertain. This exploratory randomized, sham-controlled trial will investigate three doses of PBMT-sMF in 20 women with rheumatoid arthritis affecting both hands. Participants will receive active treatment or sham twice weekly for four weeks. The hypothesis is that active treatment may reduce pain and improve clinical outcomes compared with placebo, with responses varying according to the dose applied. The objective is to explore changes in pain, disease activity, physical function, inflammatory markers, and hand temperature in women with rheumatoid arthritis , assessed before treatment, at the end of treatment, and four weeks later. The findings will help inform the design of future trials.
primary_outcomes: Change in Hand Joint Pain Intensity
title: Photobiomodulation Therapy Combined With Static Magnetic Field for Rheumatoid Arthritis of the Hands

brief_summary:
The aim of this observational study is to investigate and compare changes in salivary composition among orthodontic patients treated with different types of functional appliances, specifically acrylic-based activator appliances with metal components and prefabricated functional appliances (trainers).

Unstimulated whole saliva samples are collected via the spitting method from patients undergoing routine orthodontic treatment at the Department of Orthodontics. The study evaluates salivary biomarkers that have previously shown alterations during fixed orthodontic therapy-including total protein, calcium, amylase, glucose, myeloperoxidase, lactate dehydrogenase, secretory Immunoglobulin A (sIgA), cortisol, antioxidants, and C-reactive protein (CRP)-as well as metabolic and inflammatory markers such as insulin, insulin autoantibodies (IAA), Apolipoprotein A-I, Adiponectin, human fatty acid-binding protein 1 (FABP-1), TNF-alpha, IL-1 beta, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, MCP-1, and Melanin-Concentrating Hormone (MCH).

The findings are expected to support the broader clinical application of non-invasive salivary diagnostics in young orthodontic patients, thereby improving patient compliance.
primary_outcomes: Change in Saliva Insulin and PACAP Concetration
title: A Comparative Study of the Effects of Orthodontic Functional Appliances on Salivary Parameters

brief_summary: This Research aims to compare the effects of Bowen technique along with post isometric relaxation on pain, range of motion and hamstring tightness in non specific low back pain. It will evaluate whether the combination of both techniques is more effective in non specific low back pain than individual effect. Although previous studies have investigated these techniques individually and compared their effects , limited evidence is available regarding their combined effectiveness in patient with non specific low back pain. This Research aims to provide evidence for improving patient outcomes and quality of life through effective rehabilitation strategies
interventions: Group A Post Isometric Relaxation and Conventional treatment
Group B Bowen Technique + Post isometric relaxation
title: Effects of Bowen Technique Along With Post Isometric Relaxation in Non Specific Low Back Pain

brief_summary: Fixed orthodontic appliances increase plaque accumulation, gingival inflammation, white spot lesions and treatment-related pain. This three-arm, parallel-group randomised controlled trial compared fluoride, herbal and hydroxyapatite toothpastes (Pasta del Capitano) head-to-head in 120 orthodontic patients aged 15-25 years with metal fixed appliances in both arches (40 per group). Participants used the assigned toothpaste alone for the first three months; the same fluoride mouthwash was then added for all groups during months 4-6. We assessed plaque index, gingival index, tooth pain (visual analogue scale), white spot lesions (enamel decalcification index), and patient satisfaction at baseline and monthly for six months (satisfaction at 3 and 6 months). All 120 patients completed the trial. No between-group differences were found during the toothpaste-only phase; from month 4, the groups diverged, with the hydroxyapatite regimen associated with the lowest plaque and gingival scores, fewest white spot lesions, least pain and highest satisfaction, and the herbal regimen intermediate for most outcomes. Because all groups received the same mouthwash in months 4-6, the later differences reflect the combined regimens rather than the toothpaste alone.
title: Fluoride, Herbal, and Hydroxyapatite Toothpastes in Fixed Orthodontic Patients

brief_summary:
This study will compare pain after two ways of placing the upper abdominal port during laparoscopic gallbladder removal. A port is a short tube that allows the surgeon to pass instruments through a small opening. In both groups, the surgeon will remove the gallbladder through this opening.

Each participant will have an equal chance of receiving either technique. In one group, the surgeon will make a lengthwise opening in the band of tissue that runs down the middle of the abdomen (the linea alba). In the other group, the surgeon will use the standard technique, choosing the direction of the opening based on the patient's anatomy and the surgeon's usual practice.

The main outcome is the pain participants report at this opening 24 hours after surgery. The study team will also record how much pain medicine participants receive, including opioids, and check the wound one week after surgery.
title: Pain After Two Techniques for Placing the Upper Abdominal Port During Laparoscopic Gallbladder Removal

brief_summary: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune condition characterised by persistent joint inflammation, pain, swelling, and impaired physical function. When multiple joints are affected, these symptoms can interfere with everyday activities. Photobiomodulation therapy combined with a static magnetic field (PBMT-sMF) may influence inflammatory processes and pain, but its effects when applied to regions away from the affected joints remain uncertain. This exploratory randomized, sham-controlled trial will investigate PBMT-sMF in 10 women with rheumatoid arthritis involving the hands and at least one other joint. Participants will receive active treatment or sham twice weekly for four weeks, with applications over the cervical lymph node regions, sternum, spleen region, and diaphragm region. The hypothesis is that active PBMT-sMF may reduce pain and influence inflammatory and immune-related markers compared with sham. The objective is to explore changes in pain, disease activity, physical function, inflammatory and immune-related blood markers, and skin temperature over affected joints. Assessments will be performed before treatment, at the end of treatment, and four weeks later. The findings will support the planning of future trials.
title: Photobiomodulation Therapy Combined With Static Magnetic Field for Pain and Immune Response in Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary:
Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) are multifactorial musculoskeletal conditions affecting the temporomandibular joint, the masticatory muscles and associated structures, and are characterized by pain, limited mandibular range of motion and impaired mandibular function. Because of the anatomical, neurophysiological and biomechanical connections between the temporomandibular system and the cervical region, TMD may also affect mandibular and cervical sensorimotor function and postural control. However, few studies have assessed mandibular proprioception, cervical proprioception and dynamic postural control together in the same sample.

The aim of this cross-sectional case-control study is to compare individuals with TMD and healthy controls in terms of mandibular proprioception, cervical proprioception, mandibular and cervical range of motion and dynamic postural control. A secondary aim is to examine the relationships between these parameters and pain intensity, symptom severity, mandibular range of motion and mandibular functional limitation in individuals with TMD.

Adults aged 18 to 45 years with pain-related TMD (myalgia and/or arthralgia) diagnosed according to the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD) Axis I protocol, and age- and sex-similar healthy controls without TMD, will be included. All participants will be assessed in a single session. Mandibular proprioception will be assessed with a mandibular joint position sense test, cervical proprioception with the cervical joint position error test, and dynamic postural control with the Y Balance Test. Mandibular and cervical range of motion, pain intensity, chronic pain severity, TMD symptom severity, mandibular functional limitation, cervical disability and physical activity level will also be assessed.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Do individuals with TMD differ from healthy controls in mandibular proprioception, cervical proprioception, mandibular and cervical range of motion and dynamic postural control? In individuals with TMD, are mandibular and cervical proprioception and dynamic postural control associated with pain intensity, symptom severity, mandibular range of motion and mandibular functional limitation?
title: Mandibular and Cervical Proprioception and Dynamic Balance in Temporomandibular Disorders

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter, open-label, dose-escalation Phase I study using a Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) design. The study will evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of circular RNA-HM2002 injection administered as a single transendocardial myocardial injection in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) who are refractory to optimal medical therapy and unsuitable for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

Three dose levels (5 mg, 15 mg, and 30 mg) are planned, with 3 participants per dose level and a total planned enrollment of at least 9 participants. The primary objectives are to evaluate safety and to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).

Dose escalation decisions will be made by a Safety Review Committee (SRC) according to predefined BOIN rules with a target toxicity probability of 25%. Dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) will be assessed during the 28-day observation period after administration. All participants will be followed for 6 months after administration for safety and preliminary efficacy assessments.
primary_outcomes: incidence of adverse events (AEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), and major adverse cardiovascular events
title: A Phase I Clinical Study of HM2002 Via Transendocardial Myocardial Injection for the Treatment of Chronic Coronary Syndrome

brief_summary:
This study is a retrospective, single-center cohort study designed to evaluate the safety and feasibility of pancreatectomy with arterial resection and reconstruction (ARR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAT) in patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC).

Ten consecutive patients who underwent this complex surgical procedure at our institution between August 2024 and January 2026 will be analyzed. Data will be collected from electronic medical records and imaging systems, including patient demographics, neoadjuvant regimens, surgical details (such as pancreatic resection type, graft type, and reconstruction technique), pathology results, imaging follow-up, and perioperative complications.

The primary outcomes to be assessed are the perioperative complication rate (graded by Clavien-Dindo, focusing on Grade ≥ IIIa within 90 days) and the R0 resection rate. Secondary outcomes include graft patency (assessed by CT angiography at 1 day, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively), overall survival, and postoperative pancreatic fistula, delayed gastric emptying, and post-pancreatectomy hemorrhage as defined by the ISGPS.

This study aims to provide clinical evidence to guide surgical decision-making, particularly regarding the selection of vascular grafts and patient selection for this highly complex procedure.
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
title: Safety and Feasibility of Pancreatectomy With Arterial Resection and Reconstruction After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy for Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary: A fall in body temperature is common during liver transplantation. This single-center retrospective cohort study examines the association between the timing of forced-air warming during routine clinical care and intraoperative hypothermic burden. The cohort includes 294 adult orthotopic liver transplant recipients: 141 started forced-air warming before anesthesia induction and 153 after induction. Both groups also received circulating-water warming. Warming timing was determined by the clinical medical and nursing team or routine workflows, rather than assigned by this study. The primary outcome is cumulative exposure to core temperatures below 36.0 degrees Celsius, quantified as the area under the temperature-deficit versus time curve. Secondary and exploratory analyses address sustained hypothermia, core-temperature trajectories, and, where supported by available records, hemodynamics around graft reperfusion and postoperative outcomes. All scheduled follow-up was completed on 11 November 2026.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Intraoperative Hypothermic Burden Below 36.0 Degrees Celsius
title: Timing of Forced-Air Warming and Hypothermia During Liver Transplantation

brief_summary: The present study aims to assess whether a behavioural intervention can lead to increased and sustained flavonoid consumption. The investigators will specifically test whether knowledge of the benefits of flavonoid intake for protection against mental stress (Stress condition) or knowledge of the acute benefits of flavonoid intake (Acute condition) will result in higher intake of flavonoids compared to knowledge of the long-term impact of flavonoid intake for cardiovascular and brain health (Control). The investigators will further assess whether changes in flavonoid intake is accompanied by changes in other aspects of the diet (macro and micronutrients) as well as improvements in vascular and brain physiology. The first research hypothesis is that participants who receive specific nutritional information about the immediate (acute) effects of flavonoid intake will increase their flavonoid intake at 1 week and 4 weeks in comparison to those who receive general information about the benefits of flavonoid intake for health (control group). Likewise, participants who receive stress-specific flavonoid information will increase their flavonoid intake at 1 week and 4 weeks overall, and around stressful periods, compared to those who receive general information about the benefits of flavonoid intake for health (control group). A third hypothesis is that participants with higher daily flavonoid intake after 4 weeks will show greater endothelial function and lower declines in endothelial dysfunction in the context of stress (increased resilience to stress).
title: A Behavioural Intervention Study To Increase Flavonoid Consumption

brief_summary: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a non-progressive neurodevelopmental disorder affecting movement, posture, and balance, with spastic diplegia being a common subtype marked by trunk weakness and impaired postural control. Whole Body Vibration (WBV) therapy is designed to enhance neuromuscular activation, core strength, and balance in children with cerebral palsy by stimulating sensory receptors and reflex pathways. This randomized controlled trial will be conducted at Sehat Medical Complex and PSRD, Lahore, on 30 participants divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group will receive core stability exercises combined with WBV, while the control group will receive core stability exercises alone. Trunk control and energy expenditure will be assessed over 10 months, and data will be analyzed using SPSS version 23.0.
primary_outcomes: Change in Trunk Control Measurement Scale (TCMS) score from baseline to 12 weeks Primary Outcome Measure: Primary Outcome Measure:
title: Effects of Core Stability on Trunk Control in CP Children

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of retlirafusp alfa plus chemotherapy as induction therapy followed by standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy in unresectable stage III NSCLC.
title: A Study of Retlirafusp Alfa Plus Chemotherapy Induction Followed by Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy in Patients With Unresectable Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary: Symbiotic-GU-07 is a Phase 3, double-blind study evaluating the investigational PD-1 × VEGF bispecific antibody PF-08634404 in combination with enfortumab vedotin (EV) compared to enfortumab vedotin (EV) with Pembrolizumab in adults with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma. The study evaluates safety, antitumor activity, and pharmacokinetics.
title: Symbiotic-GU-07-A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine PF-08634404 In Combination With Enfortumab Vedotin Compared to Enfortumab Vedotin in Combination With Pembrolizumab in Adult Participants With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Cancer.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial compared the effects of physiotherapist-supervised online telerehabilitation and educational material-supported home exercises in office workers with nonspecific neck pain. The study included 40 participants aged 18-55 years, randomly allocated to a telerehabilitation group (n=20) or a home exercise group (n=20). Both groups completed a six-week exercise program consisting of three sessions per week. Pain intensity, neck disability, sleep quality, kinesiophobia, and health-related quality of life were assessed at baseline and after six weeks. The study aimed to evaluate differences in clinical outcomes between supervised online rehabilitation and independently performed home exercises.
primary_outcomes: Change in Neck Pain Intensity Assessed by the Numeric Rating Scale
title: Supervised Online Telerehabilitation Versus Home Exercise for Nonspecific Neck Pain in Office Workers

brief_summary: This study aimed to determine whether bougie size (40 and 52French) matters in laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Reporting Postoperative Nausea
title: In Laparoscopic Fundoplication, Does a Bougie Size Matters?

brief_summary: The study design will be a quasi-experimental design conducted over ten months in pediatric physiotherapy department of sundus foundation. It will include 22 children aged 8 to 12 years with congenital hemophilia A and with a joint status score greater than 5 on the Hemophilia Joint Health Score (HJHS). Outcomes will be assessed using Hemophilia joint health score and Pediatric quality of life inventory to measure joint health and quality of life . Ethical approval will be obtained from the Research Ethical Committee of Riphah International University, Lahore, and data will be analyzed using SPSS version 27.0.
interventions: RICE Protocol+ Structured Physical Therapy Program
title: Effects of Structured Physical Therapy Program on Joint Health in Hemophilia

brief_summary:
The goal of this single-centre, retrospective-prospective observational case-control study is to assess changes in cardiorespiratory fitness following supervised exercise-based prehabilitation and to compare postoperative clinical outcomes in adults aged 18-85 years with multiple comorbidities (Charlson Comorbidity Index \[CCI\]\>5) who are scheduled for major pulmonary resection for suspected primary or secondary pulmonary malignancy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How does maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max), measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), change between baseline (T0) and completion of prehabilitation (T1)?
* Do the incidence of postoperative complications, postoperative length of stay, duration of pleural air leakage, pleural fluid drainage volume and chest-drain duration differ between patients receiving prehabilitation and those receiving standard perioperative care? Researchers will compare patients receiving care through an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway that includes supervised exercise-based prehabilitation with patients receiving standard perioperative care without prehabilitation. Matching analyses will be used to account for differences in recorded patient characteristics.

Participants will:

* Undergo preoperative clinical assessment. Patients assessed for prehabilitation will also undergo functional assessments, as clinically appropriate, including CPET, the treadmill six-minute walk test (T-6MWT), spirometry, bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), handgrip dynamometry and questionnaires.
* If clinically eligible and willing, undertake a structured, adapted and supervised exercise programme comprising at least five sessions of approximately 60 minutes each over at least three weeks, followed by functional reassessment before surgery.
* Undergo their planned pulmonary resection if surgery proceeds as indicated and receive appropriate perioperative clinical care. Postoperative outcomes will be recorded from clinical records for participants whose surgery meets the study protocol's criteria.
* If they have completed prehabilitation, remain clinically stable and choose to continue adapted physical exercise after surgery, they may undergo an optional functional reassessment approximately 50-90 days after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Change in Maximal Oxygen Uptake Measured by Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing
title: Structured and Adapted Exercise Prehabilitation Before Pulmonary Resection in Patients With Multiple Comorbidities

brief_summary: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) can be raised by benign conditions such as prostatitis, which may lead to unnecessary prostate biopsies. Glucose in the urine (glucosuria), most often due to diabetes or SGLT2-inhibitor treatment, can cause urinary symptoms similar to prostatitis. This study examines whether glucosuria and prostatitis are associated with MRI findings and prostate cancer detection in men with urinary symptoms and a PSA level between 3 and 10 ng/mL. Men with glucosuria first receive glycemic control; men without glucosuria, or with persistent symptoms, receive a 4-week course of ciprofloxacin and alfuzosin. All men then undergo multiparametric MRI and prostate biopsy, and cancer and clinically significant cancer rates are compared according to glucosuria and histological prostatitis.
primary_outcomes: Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer Detection Rate
title: Glucosuria and Histological Prostatitis in Men With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and PSA 3-10 ng/mL

brief_summary:
Parkinson's disease (PD) causes progressive motor impairments that reduce mobility, increase fall risk, and negatively affect quality of life despite pharmacological and surgical treatments. Dance therapy has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological rehabilitation approach, although current evidence remains limited.

The ParkiDanse program combines movement, rhythm, vocalization, and playful imaginative elements to enhance motor function, engagement, and self-confidence. The RéSoNAnce study is a cluster randomized controlled trial comparing ParkiDanse with classical dance in people with PD. The primary outcome is the between-group difference in the Mini-BESTest score at 3 months, a validated measure of dynamic balance and postural stability that is sensitive to rehabilitation interventions.
title: Rehabilitation Through Music and Dance in Parkinson's Disease: Evaluation of the PARKIDANSE Program

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to compare unilateral and conventional bilateral spinal anesthesia in elderly patients (aged 65 years and older) undergoing elective open unilateral inguinal hernia repair. The choice of spinal anesthesia technique is made by the attending anesthesiologist as part of routine clinical care, and patients are observed in two groups: unilateral spinal anesthesia (Group U) and bilateral spinal anesthesia (Group B). The study compares the two techniques in terms of intraoperative complications (hypotension, bradycardia, vasopressor and sedation requirement), block characteristics, and postoperative complications (nausea and vomiting, post-dural puncture headache, urinary retention, and time to first analgesic requirement). It is hypothesized that unilateral spinal anesthesia provides a more stable hemodynamic profile and lower incidence of hypotension and bradycardia in elderly patients.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Intraoperative Hypotension
title: Unilateral Versus Bilateral Spinal Anesthesia in Elderly Patients: Intraoperative and Postoperative Complications

brief_summary: The study will use a randomized clinical trial design conducted over ten months in special education schools. It will include 22 children aged 9-18 years with Down Syndrome selected after eligibility screening and guardian consent. Outcomes will be assessed using BOT-2, Pediatric Berg Balance (PBS), Scale ,Timed Up and Go Test (TUG), and 10-Meter Walk Test to measure sensory motor skills, balance, gait parameters Ethical approval will be obtained from the Research Ethical Committee of Riphah International University, Lahore, and data will be analyzed using SPSS version 26.0.
title: Comparative Effects of Sensory Motor Training and Bulgarian Bag Exercises

brief_summary: CRANIOPRO is a single-center, prospective observational cohort study conducted at Hospital Universitário Getúlio Vargas (HUGV) in Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil. It follows adult patients who have sustained traumatic brain injury (TBI), undergone decompressive craniectomy, and are scheduled for elective cranioplasty (skull reconstruction). The study aims to provide an integrated assessment of post-cranioplasty recovery by evaluating cognition (MoCA and Neupsilin), motor and global function, masticatory function (electromyography, bite force, mouth opening, and pain), advanced neuroimaging (diffusion tensor imaging \[DTI\] and the ALPS index), and digital biomarkers collected using a smartwatch and smart ring during the four weeks following surgery, including heart rate, heart rate variability, sleep, physical activity, and temperature.
primary_outcomes: Change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) total score
title: CRANIOPRO - Prospective Cohort of Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury Undergoing Cranioplasty: Integration of Cognition, Masticatory Function, Advanced Neuroimaging and Digital Biomarkers

brief_summary: This randomized clinical trial will be conducted at The Light School, Sialkot, among children with Down syndrome aged 9-12 years of both genders who can stand and walk independently. Participants will be randomly divided into resistance-training and aerobic-training groups to improve muscular endurance and postural control. Pre- and post-intervention outcomes will be assessed using the PAS-DS, 20-Meter Shuttle Run (Beep) Test, and 6-Minute Walk Test. Children with visual or hearing impairments, non-verbal or non-ambulatory children, and those requiring parental involvement will be excluded. Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 26.0.
primary_outcomes: Postural Assessment Scale for Children with Down Syndrome (PAS-D)
title: Effects of Resistance Training and Aerobic Training in Down Syndrome

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of video watching and palm stimulator use on pain, fear, and anxiety levels during dressing procedures in children who have undergone liver transplantation.

Dressing changes can be painful and stressful for children. Non-pharmacological methods, such as distraction techniques, may help reduce negative emotions and improve children's comfort during medical procedures. In this study, participating children will undergo routine dressing procedures and dressing procedures with distraction interventions (video watching or palm stimulator). Pain, fear, and anxiety levels will be assessed before, during, and after the procedure using validated scales. In addition, video recordings focused only on facial expressions will be evaluated by an independent observer. The findings of this study may contribute to the development of evidence-based nursing interventions to improve procedural comfort in pediatric liver transplant recipients.
title: THE EFFECT OF PALM STIMULATOR AND VIDEO INTERVENTIONS ON PAIN, FEAR, AND STRESS DURING DRESSING CHANGES IN CHILDREN WHO HAVE UNDERGONE LIVER TRANSPLANTATION

brief_summary: This is a single-center, prospective, observational cohort study. Approximately 1,000 patients undergoing bariatric and metabolic surgery at the Department of Gastrointestinal Surgery, the Second Qilu Hospital of Shandong University, will be consecutively enrolled, without randomization, blinding, or a parallel control group. Participants will be followed up for a maximum of 5 years from enrollment. Clinical data and biological samples will be systematically collected at preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative time points, with outcomes including weight loss, metabolic improvement, and long-term complications being observed.
lead_sponsor: The Second Hospital of Shandong University
title: A Prospective Cohort Study of Long-term Outcomes Following Bariatric and Metabolic Surgery

brief_summary: Many people with ulcerative colitis (UC) continue to experience symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloating, and bowel urgency, even when there is little or no active inflammation in their intestines. Researchers believe that communication between the brain, nervous system, and gut may play an important role in these ongoing symptoms. The purpose of this study is to determine whether 8 weeks of non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation changes brain activity and communication within networks that regulate digestion, pain, and body functions such as heart rate. Researchers will also evaluate whether these changes are associated with improvements in gastrointestinal symptoms, nervous system function, and markers of inflammation. Participation in this study involves random assignment to a study group for 8 weeks and then followed for an additional 4 weeks after completing the intervention. The study aims to assess the effects of the intervention using brain imaging, wearable device measurements, laboratory tests for inflammation, and questionnaires about symptoms and quality of life. The goal is to better understand how the brain-gut connection contributes to persistent symptoms in ulcerative colitis and whether non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation may help improve those symptoms.
conditions: Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Ulcerative Colitis Type
primary_outcomes: Change from in the CAN functional connectivity
title: nVNS Trial in UC-IBS Overlap Patients

brief_summary:
This study evaluates the feasibility and safety of combining wearable electrical muscle stimulation with physiotherapy in adults with persistent muscle weakness and walking difficulties following stroke.

A total of 90 adults aged 18-80 years with chronic post-stroke hemiparesis will participate in this prospective, randomized, assessor-blinded pilot feasibility study.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups:

1. Physiotherapy combined with wearable electrical muscle stimulation using the E-Fit CONNECT LIGHT device.
2. Standardized physiotherapy without electrical stimulation.
3. Guideline-concordant usual rehabilitation care.

Participants in the first two groups will receive three supervised 40-minute treatment sessions per week for eight weeks, totaling 24 sessions. All participants will undergo assessments at baseline, week 8, and week 12.

The main objective is to determine whether the device-assisted rehabilitation programme can be delivered consistently and safely. The primary outcome is the proportion of participants in the device-assisted group who complete at least 20 of the 24 scheduled sessions.

Researchers will also monitor adverse events, treatment tolerability, participant retention, and completion of planned assessments.

Exploratory assessments will examine walking speed, balance, mobility, muscle strength, fatigue, perceived exertion, and heart-rate and blood-pressure responses.

This pilot study is designed to evaluate feasibility and safety-related outcomes rather than establish the effectiveness of the device. Its findings will inform the design of future clinical investigations.
title: Wearable Electrical Muscle Stimulation for Rehabilitation After Stroke

brief_summary: Ahesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder) is a painful musculoskeletal condition characterized by progressive stiffness and significant restriction of glenohumeral range of motion (ROM), often accompanied by altered scapular kinematics (scapular dyskinesis). This single-blind randomized clinical trial aims to compare the effects of Scapular Clock Training combined with a conventional physiotherapy program versus a conventional exercise program alone on pain, shoulder ROM, and functional disability in patients with adhesive capsulitis. A total of 44 participants aged 40 to 65 years with clinically diagnosed unilateral adhesive capsulitis will be recruited from RK Physio, Sialkot, and randomly allocated into two equal groups ($n = 22$ per group). Both groups will receive an identical baseline physiotherapy regimen consisting of a hot pack, therapeutic ultrasound, and Grade III/IV glenohumeral joint mobilizations. Group A (Experimental) will additionally perform multidirectional Scapular Clock Training alongside a structured conventional exercise program, while Group B (Control) will perform the conventional exercise program alone. Outcome measures including pain intensity (Numeric Pain Rating Scale), goniometric shoulder ROM, and functional disability (Shoulder Pain and Disability Index) will be evaluated at baseline, after 2 weeks, and at the completion of the 4-week intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Shoulder Pain Intensity using Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS)
Change in Shoulder Functional Disability using Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI)
title: Scapular Clock Training Versus Conventional Exercise Adhesive Capsulitis

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of electroencephalography (EEG)-guided personalized music intervention on depressive symptoms in college students. Participants will receive either conventional music intervention or EEG-guided personalized music intervention. Depressive symptoms will be assessed before and after the intervention. EEG, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and data from wearable wristbands will also be collected. This study will investigate whether EEG-guided personalized music intervention provides additional benefits compared with conventional music intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in derepssion using Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)
title: Personalized Music Intervention for Depressive Adolescent Guided by EEG Gamma Oscillation Feedback

brief_summary:
This is an open-label Phase 1/2a study evaluating the safety and preliminary antitumor activity of Bria-BRES+ cellular immunotherapy in adults with recurrent metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable breast cancer that has progressed following prior therapies.

Phase 1 will evaluate escalating doses of Bria-BRES+ to characterize safety and determine the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D). Additional Bria-BRES+ cell lines may then be evaluated at the RP2D. Phase 2a will further evaluate Bria-BRES+ at the RP2D, with treatment selected to optimize human leukocyte antigen (HLA) matching when possible.

The primary objective is to evaluate the safety of Bria-BRES+ cellular immunotherapy. Secondary and exploratory objectives include evaluating tumor response, progression-free survival, overall survival, immune responses, cytokine pharmacokinetics, and patient or tumor characteristics that may predict response to treatment.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and Severity of Adverse Events and Serious Adverse Events
title: Bria-BRES+ Immunotherapy for Recurrent or Metastatic Breast Cancer

brief_summary: Low back pain (LBP) is a global disability cause, affecting millions and leading to reduced productivity and increased sick leave. The aim is to evaluate the effects of stecco-fascial mobilization compared to ART on pain, range of motion (ROM), and functional disability in chronic non-specific LBP patients.
title: Effects Of Stecco-Fascial Mobilization Versus Active Release Technique in Patients With Chronic Non-Specific Low Back Pain

brief_summary:
This study compared three ways of adjusting a device used to widen a narrow upper jaw in people aged 15 to 20. The main question was whether the adjustment schedule affected the roots of the upper teeth or the size of the upper airway.

All participants received an expander held in place by small screws in the bone at the roof of the mouth. Each participant was assigned by chance to one of three groups. In the semirapid group, participants turned the expander screw only in the direction that widened the jaw. In the polycyclic and modified polycyclic groups, participants turned the screw in both directions, following a different schedule in each group.

Researchers compared 3D dental scans taken before treatment and after the expander had held the jaw in its widened position. They measured changes in tooth root length and volume, upper airway size, and jaw width. They also assessed whether expansion was successful, measured the force needed to turn the screw, and asked participants about pain and how treatment affected daily life.
primary_outcomes: Change in Total Maxillary Tooth Volume
Change in Transverse Width of the Hard Palate
title: Investigation of the Effects of Bone-anchored Maxillary Expansion Devices Activated Via Different Protocols

brief_summary: This is a randomized, open-label, single-dose, two-period crossover study to compare the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles of test human insulin isophane suspension 30R and reference Humulin® 70/30 following subcutaneous injection in healthy adult subjects. Pharmacodynamic evaluation will be performed using the euglycemic glucose clamp technique. Safety will also be assessed.
title: A PK/PD Study of Human Insulin Isophane Suspension 30R (Test vs Humulin® 70/30) in Healthy Subjects

brief_summary:
Frailty is a multidimensional geriatric condition associated with reduced muscle strength and power, impaired physical function, loss of independence, and increased risk of adverse health outcomes. The pre-frail stage is particularly relevant because it represents a potentially reversible phase in which targeted exercise interventions may prevent or delay progression toward established frailty.

The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of low-load resistance training combined with blood flow restriction (LL-BFR) on lower-limb muscle power and physical function in community-dwelling pre-frail older adults. Secondary objectives include assessing its effects on muscle strength, physical performance, gait speed, frailty status, reversal from pre-frailty to robustness, functional independence, health-related quality of life, adherence, and safety.

Participants aged 65 years or older and classified as pre-frail according to the Fried Frailty Phenotype (1-2 criteria) will be randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three intervention groups: (1) conventional resistance training (CRT), (2) low-load resistance training with effective blood flow restriction (LL-BFR), or (3) low-load resistance training with sham blood flow restriction (LL-sham BFR). The minimum required sample is 84 evaluable participants (28 per group), with recruitment increased to approximately 105 participants to account for potential losses.

All groups will complete a 16-week supervised exercise program consisting of two non-consecutive sessions per week. CRT will be performed at approximately 65% of one-repetition maximum (1RM), whereas both low-load groups will train at approximately 30% of 1RM. In the LL-BFR group, cuff pressure will be individualized at 65% of limb occlusion pressure, while the sham group will receive a fixed low pressure of 20 mmHg.

Outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16. The primary outcome will be relative lower-limb sit-to-stand muscle power derived from the five-times sit-to-stand test. Secondary outcomes will include leg-press strength, Short Physical Performance Battery score, gait speed, Fried frailty criteria, functional independence, and patient-reported health-related quality of life.

This three-arm design will allow the specific effects of BFR to be distinguished from those of low-load exercise alone and from conventional higher-load resistance training, providing clinically relevant evidence on whether LL-BFR may represent an effective and feasible strategy for improving physical function and reversing pre-frailty in older adults.
interventions: Low-Load Resistance Training with Blood Flow Restriction
Low-Load Resistance Training with Sham Blood Flow Restriction
title: Blood Flow Restriction Training in Pre-Frail Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This in vitro study aims to assess and compare the marginal adaptation and internal fit of inlay zirconia fixed bridges fabricated using intraoral scanning and extraoral scanning. The study will be performed on a Nissen typodont model. Prepared teeth replacing a missing lower first molar will be scanned using intraoral and extraoral scanning techniques. The resulting zirconia fixed bridges will be evaluated for marginal adaptation as the primary outcome and internal fit as the secondary outcome using a stereomicroscope.
lead_sponsor: October University for Modern Sciences and Arts
primary_outcomes: Marginal adaptation of the inlay zirconia fixed bridge
title: Assessment of Internal Fit and Marginal Adaptation of Inlay Zirconia Fixed Bridge Using Intraoral Versus Extraoral Scanner

brief_summary:
The goal of this Pilot study is to examine the possibility and safety of using Artificial Intelligence (AI) conversational tools (chatbots) to help improve individuals' mental well-being. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How safe is an AI chatbot in use for a study about mental wellness?
* How usable is the platform for this study?
* How willing are participants to remain and complete the study?
* What was the user experience like?
* Do they show any signs of dependancy on the chatbot?

Researchers will compare participants who did the mental wellness sessions with the chosen chatbot, Doro, to those who used common self-help materials to examine the safety and effectiveness of AI chatbots in supporting mental wellness.

Participants will:

* Have a pre-study mental wellness assessment.
* Be divided into 2 groups: the experimental group and the control group.
* The experimental group will interact with the Doro AI Chatbot.
* The control group will interact with the self-help work materials.
* Have a mid-point mental wellness assessment.
* Have a mental wellness survey after all the sessions, and
* Have a final interview with one of the researchers.
interventions: Self-help reading materials with reflection exercises
primary_outcomes: Percentage of new chat logs reviewed by the research team within 24 hours
Completion rate of study assessment instruments
Serious adverse events detected by chat-log review and managed using the safety protocol
Participant experience and signs of dependence, assessed by interview
title: Feasibility and Safety of an AI Chatbot Compared to Self-Help Materials for University Student Well-Being: A Pilot Study

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility of a 10-week, home-based telerehabilitation program called DUMFET for premature infants aged 4-12 months who are at risk of developmental delays. The program includes play-based activities designed to support motor, sensory, social, and emotional development, with active participation from parents or caregivers. Infant development and caregiver outcomes will be assessed before and after the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility, Acceptability, Satisfaction, and Safety of Tele-Rehabilitation
Test of Sensory Functions in Infants (TSFI)
title: Feasibility of DUMFET-Based Telerehabilitation for Preterm Infants at Risk of Developmental Delays

brief_summary:
Postoperative recurrence of bladder cancer requires regular clinical surveillance. This study will evaluate urinary extracellular vesicle (EV) N-glycan profiles for assessing postoperative recurrence risk and detecting recurrence during follow-up. EVs are membrane-bound particles released by cells, and N-glycans are carbohydrate structures attached to proteins. The study will assess whether these profiles are associated with subsequent recurrence and whether an EV-derived glycan score can identify recurrence present at the time of urine collection.

The study has two components at Changhai Hospital. The retrospective component will assess eligible patients from an existing pool of 121 patients with bladder cancer. Their urine sugar profiles collected before surgery will be linked to treatment and follow-up records. Patients treated with bladder-preserving surgery and those treated with removal of the bladder will be analyzed separately. The study will also explore whether adding sugar-profile information to clinical factors improves prediction of recurrence within 12 months in an appropriate bladder-preserving subgroup.

The prospective component plans to include 156 new adults with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer after completion of tumor resection with no known remaining tumor. Urine will be collected before the initial resection and approximately 3 and 6 months after completion of local treatment. A previously developed eight-sugar score, called EVGScore, will be evaluated using a fixed calculation method and threshold.

The main prospective question is how often EVGScore correctly identifies patients who have recurrence at the 3-month assessment. The study will also assess false-positive results, compare the score with urine cytology, which examines cells in urine, and describe changes in urine sugar patterns over time.

Recurrence will be assessed independently of the research sugar-test results using standard clinical examinations. This observational study does not assign treatment. Research test results will not replace recommended examinations, delay care, or determine treatment.
primary_outcomes: Time to first intravesical recurrence in the historical bladder-preserving NMIBC subgroup
Sensitivity of EVGScore for contemporaneous intravesical recurrence at 3 months
title: Urinary Extracellular Vesicle (EV) Glycan Profiles for Assessing Bladder Cancer Recurrence After Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether a training module on feeding behaviour, the Feeding Behaviour Module for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (FBMCASD), helps healthcare professionals in residential autism care centres in Amman, Jordan, manage feeding problems among the children they care for. The study includes healthcare professionals working in these centres and children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) aged 6 to 15 years who show food selectivity.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the FBMCASD improve healthcare professionals' beliefs, attitudes and feeding practices regarding nutrition and feeding problems in children with ASD?
* Does the FBMCASD reduce problematic mealtime behaviour (including food selectivity) among children with ASD?
* Does the FBMCASD improve children's dietary intake and anthropometric measures (weight, height and body mass index)?

Researchers will compare one centre that received the FBMCASD with another centre that continued its usual (standard) care.

Healthcare professionals in the intervention centre:

* Attend three weekly interactive training sessions covering feeding challenges in ASD, nutritional principles, behavioural feeding strategies, and feeding assessment and monitoring
* Apply the learned strategies during routine care of the children
* Complete a beliefs, attitudes and feeding practices questionnaire at baseline, 8 weeks and 20 weeks after the intervention

For children in both centres, mealtime behaviour (Brief Autism Mealtime Behaviour Inventory, BAMBI), 24-hour dietary recall and weight and height are assessed at the same three time points.
interventions: Feeding Behaviour Module for Children with ASD (FBMCASD)
primary_outcomes: Change in Healthcare Professionals' Beliefs, Attitudes and Feeding Practices Score
Change in Children's Mealtime Behaviour (Brief Autism Mealtime Behaviour Inventory, BAMBI) Total Score
title: Feeding Behaviour Module for Healthcare Professionals Caring for Children With Autism in Amman, Jordan

brief_summary: Lumbar radiculopathy is a common neuromusculoskeletal condition characterized by radiating leg pain, sensory disturbances, muscle weakness, and restricted movement due to compression or irritation of the lumbar nerve roots. It significantly affects functional ability and quality of life and is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Conservative physiotherapy management is considered the first line of treatment for lumbar radiculopathy, with increasing emphasis on exercise-based and manual therapy interventions.
title: Effects of Neurodynamic Mobilization With or Without Motor Control Training on Pain, Range of Motion and Muscle Strength With Lumbar Radiculopathy.

brief_summary: Overnight healthcare workers are routinely exposed to physiological and occupational stressors that may negatively affect cardiovascular and endothelial function. Chronic overnight work is associated with circadian disruption, sleep restriction, autonomic dysregulation, oxidative stress, and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Endothelial dysfunction may occur before clinically apparent cardiovascular disease and is characterized in part by impaired nitric oxide (NO) mediated vasodilation. Acute overnight work may also affect vascular function. Previous investigations in medical personnel have reported reductions in brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) following a single overnight shift, suggesting that measurable endothelial impairment may occur during the immediate post-shift period. NO is an important signaling molecule involved in the regulation of vascular tone, blood flow, and blood pressure. Under normal conditions, endothelial NO synthase produces NO from L-arginine. However, oxidative stress and impaired endothelial function can reduce NO production and bioavailability. Dietary nitrate provides an alternative pathway for NO production through the nitrate-nitrite-NO pathway. Following ingestion, nitrate is absorbed into the circulation and a portion is concentrated in saliva, where oral nitrate-reducing bacteria convert nitrate to nitrite. Nitrite can then be further reduced to biologically active NO. This pathway may remain functional under conditions in which endogenous endothelial NO production is impaired. Dietary nitrate supplementation has been investigated as a nutritional strategy for supporting cardiovascular and vascular function. Previous studies using nitrate-rich vegetables have demonstrated increases in circulating nitrate and nitrite, reductions in blood pressure, and improvements in endothelial function. Arugula is a nitrate-rich leafy green vegetable and contains one of the highest reported nitrate concentrations among commonly consumed leafy green and cruciferous vegetables. However, most dietary nitrate research has focused on beetroot-derived supplementation, and arugula remains underrepresented. Acute arugula extract supplementation may therefore provide a practical source of exogenous nitrate for examining vascular responses during the post-shift period. The purpose of this study is to determine the acute effects of arugula extract (AE) supplementation on cardiovascular and endothelial function following an overnight shift in healthcare workers. Specifically, the study will determine whether acute AE supplementation: 1) improves FMD, 2) increases circulating nitrate, nitrite, and total NO metabolites, and 3) reduces blood pressure compared with a post-shift control condition. Heart rate will also be assessed throughout each condition. We hypothesize that AE supplementation will increase circulating NO metabolites, improve FMD, and reduce blood pressure following an overnight healthcare shift.
title: Nurses Aid: The Effects of Arugula Extract On Cardiovascular and Endothelial Function In Overnight Healthcare Workers: A Pilot Study

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the intervention effect of drinking mineral water rich in bicarbonate on the natural course of kidney stones in asymptomatic patients.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will drink 1.0 liter of bicarbonate-rich mineral water every day for 12 months. The other group will drink 1.0 liter of regular drinking water every day for the same period. Both groups will be encouraged to drink extra plain water as needed.

Researchers will compare the two groups to see if the mineral water reduces the chance of kidney stone progression. Progression means new stones appearing, existing stones getting bigger, or stones causing symptoms that need medical treatment. The study will also check changes in urine chemistry and stone density on CT scans.

Participants will visit the clinic for a kidney CT scan and urine and blood tests before the study starts. During the 12-month treatment period, the study team will call participants once a month to check how they are doing and whether they are drinking the assigned water. Every 3 months, participants will come to the clinic for urine and blood tests. A kidney CT scan will be done at month 3 and again at month 12.

Eligible participants must be at least 18 years old, have kidney stones detected by CT scan with a diameter of 15 millimeters or less, and have no history of pain, hematuria, infection or previous surgery related to the stones in the past.
lead_sponsor: The First Hospital of Jilin University
title: Effect of Bicarbonate-Rich Mineral Water on Patients With Asymptomatic Kidney Stones

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of probiotic supplementation on blood pressure regulation in adults aged 50 to 75 years.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Participants will be assigned to receive either the probiotic product Probiotic product or a matching placebo over an 8-week intervention period.

Study assessments will be conducted at baseline (Week 0), Week 4, and Week 8. Assessments will include systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), glucose metabolism indicators, blood lipid profiles, inflammatory markers, immune indicators, gut microbiota composition, gastrointestinal symptoms, and safety parameters.

The study will evaluate changes in blood pressure following probiotic supplementation and monitor the safety and tolerability of the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP) from Baseline to Week 8
Change in Diastolic Blood Pressure (DBP) from Baseline to Week 8

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether taking dexketoprofen and paracetamol together every 8 hours controls pain as well as the usual regimen of alternating dexketoprofen and paracetamol every 4 hours in adults after surgical removal of lower wisdom teeth. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the combined regimen (dexketoprofen 25 mg plus paracetamol 650 mg every 8 hours) provide pain control similar to or better than the alternating regimen (dexketoprofen 25 mg and paracetamol 1000 mg alternated every 4 hours)?
* Do the two regimens differ in the need for rescue pain medication, side effects, patient satisfaction and quality of life during the first days after surgery?

Researchers will compare the two pain medication regimens. All participants will receive active pain treatment and will have access to rescue medication if needed.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two regimens, without knowing which one they receive
* Have their lower wisdom tooth removed at the CEU Cardenal Herrera University Dental Clinic
* Take the study capsules for 5 days after surgery
* Record their pain level, any rescue medication and side effects in a diary during the 5 days after surgery
* Complete short questionnaires on anxiety before surgery and on recovery and satisfaction after surgery
* Return for suture removal 7 days after surgery
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity (Numeric Rating Scale, NRS 0-10)
title: Dexketoprofen Plus Paracetamol for Pain After Lower Wisdom Tooth Removal

brief_summary:
Bile acids are molecules made by the liver that help digest fat. They also act as signals that tell the body's tissues how to respond to food, and they are linked to liver disease and metabolic problems. Doctors can only measure bile acids in blood from an arm vein, because sampling the portal vein (the vessel carrying blood from the gut to the liver) or the liver is not done in routine care. As a result, we know very little about how bile acids are distributed between the gut and the liver, especially in healthy people.

This study will measure bile acids for the first time in several body compartments of the same healthy adult: liver tissue, portal and peripheral blood, bile, stool, and fat tissue. We will collect these samples from adults donating part of their liver at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc (Brussels). Samples are taken during the donation surgery, and the leftover liver tissue that is not used for the transplant is used for research.

The study asks two questions. How are bile acids distributed along the gut-liver pathway in a healthy liver? And can this information be used to build a mathematical model that predicts bile acid levels in the portal vein from a simple blood test? Such a tool could help doctors identify patients at risk and offer more personalized treatment.
interventions: Research sample collection during living liver donation
primary_outcomes: Concentration of bile acids in enterohepatic compartments of healthy living liver donors
title: Bile Acid Profiling in Healthy Donors

brief_summary: Thoracic surgery induces a systemic inflammatory response. Open thoracotomy is more invasive, often associated with higher levels of inflammatory biomarkers (IL 6, CRP, TNF α, procalcitonin). VATS, being minimally invasive, is hypothesized to cause less biomarker elevation, correlating with faster recovery and fewer complications. Comparing biomarker profiles between the two approaches may provide objective evidence for minimally invasive surgery benefits and guide personalized postoperative monitoring.
title: Perioperative Biomarkers in Thoracic Surgery

brief_summary:
Pancreatic masses are abnormal lumps that can form in the pancreas. They can be cancerous or non-cancerous and include several different conditions, such as pancreatic cancer, neuroendocrine tumors, cysts, and inflammation-related lumps. Telling these conditions apart is difficult, because they can look alike on scans and cause similar symptoms. Pancreatic cancer is a serious disease that is hard to find early and often comes back after surgery, so making the right diagnosis matters.

Doctors currently use imaging tests (such as CT and MRI), tissue samples, and blood tests (such as CA19-9) to judge whether a pancreatic mass is cancerous and how it may behave. Each test shows only part of the picture. Scans show the size and location of a mass but can miss tiny spread. Some tissue features are known only after a biopsy or surgery. No single blood test is accurate enough on its own.

This study will use medical information and samples from patients with pancreatic masses at our hospital. It has two parts. First, researchers will review records of patients already diagnosed or treated here from 2020 onward. Second, after the study is approved, eligible new patients will be enrolled as they come for care. The information includes medical records, imaging results, pathology reports, and records of team meetings held to plan patient care. Stored samples such as blood and tissue will also be used. Our hospital has experience in diagnosing and treating pancreatic disease and has previously studied clinical information and blood markers, which supports this work. Researchers will examine substances in the blood, including tumor DNA (cfDNA/ctDNA), which may carry clues about the disease that scans cannot show.

The main question of this study is whether combining clinical information, imaging, tissue tests, and blood markers gives a better picture than any single test alone. Researchers hope this may help classify pancreatic masses more accurately and estimate the risk of cancer and recurrence. This is an observational study: researchers will only analyze existing information and samples and will not assign any treatment or change the care patients receive.
lead_sponsor: Cancer Institute and Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: Final disease classification of pancreatic space-occupying lesions (malignant versus non-malignant)
title: Multimodal Classification and Malignant Risk Stratification of Pancreatic Space-Occupying Lesions

brief_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of virtual reality (VR)-based action observation and motor imagery (AOMI) exercises on physical fitness parameters in individuals with schizophrenia. Participants were assigned to one of three groups: individuals with schizophrenia who received VR-AOMI exercises, individuals with schizophrenia who received no intervention (control), and healthy individuals who received VR-AOMI exercises. Each participant attended two sessions approximately one month apart: an aerobic exercise session and a resistance exercise session, each delivered through VR-based action observation and motor imagery. Physical fitness measures were assessed before and after each session. The study hypothesized that VR-AOMI exercises would produce measurable acute effects on physical fitness parameters in individuals with schizophrenia, and aimed to determine whether this approach could serve as an alternative exercise method for individuals with schizophrenia, who often face barriers to traditional physical activity due to motivational and physical limitations.

brief_summary: This study looks at how eating a plant-based Mediterranean diet before surgery affects the healthy bacteria in the gut and overall health. Eating healthy foods may boost helpful gut bacteria and lower harmful bacteria. In this study, researchers will test stool samples to look at the tiny living organisms in the gut, also called the gut microbiome. This test looks only at the DNA of the gut bacteria, not a person's own human DNA. Checking these samples shows how changes in diet affect the types and behavior of gut bacteria. Personal information and privacy are kept safe throughout the study. Results from this study may help find new ways to improve health after surgery and lower the chance of cancer coming back.
primary_outcomes: Change in Log10 Collagenolytic Activity of Gut Microbiome Bacteria
title: MicrobIOme DIet For SurgerY

brief_summary:
Low blood pressure is a common side effect of spinal anesthesia during cesarean delivery. Phenylephrine is a medicine routinely given to prevent this, but the best single injected dose is not well established, especially in hospitals where continuous infusion pumps are not always available.

This randomized, double-blind study compared four doses of phenylephrine (50, 75, 100, or 125 micrograms) given into a vein immediately after spinal anesthesia in healthy women having a planned cesarean delivery. The main question was how often each dose still required additional rescue phenylephrine to treat low blood pressure before the baby was born. The study also compared the mother's blood pressure and heart rate, side effects such as nausea, vomiting and slow heart rate, and the baby's condition at birth (Apgar scores and umbilical cord blood gases).
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Requiring Rescue Phenylephrine Before Delivery
title: Four Prophylactic Phenylephrine Bolus Doses for Spinal Anesthesia Hypotension in Cesarean Delivery
